│          xs, ys = parsed_coords[i]                                           │
│          if xs and ys:                                                       │
│              xmin = int(min(xs)); ymin = int(min(ys)); xmax = int(max(xs));  │
│  ymax = int(max(ys))                                                         │
│          else:                                                               │
│              xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax = 0,0,w-1,h-1                            │
│      mask = np.zeros((h,w), dtype=np.uint8)                                  │
│      score = None                                                            │
│      sam_used = False                                                        │
│                                                                              │
│      # Try SAM if available                                                  │
│      if sam_available:                                                       │
│          try:                                                                │
│              predictor_wrapper.set_image(img_np)                             │
│              if df.loc[i, &#x27;_is_rect&#x27;]:                             │
│                  box = (xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax)                              │
│                  m, s = predictor_wrapper.predict_box(box)                   │
│              else:                                                           │
│                  # build point prompts: centroid + up to 2 evenly spaced     │
│  polygon points                                                              │
│                  if len(xs) &gt;= 1:                                         │
│                      cx = int(sum(xs)/len(xs)); cy = int(sum(ys)/len(ys))    │
│                      pts = [(cx, cy)]                                        │
│                      if len(xs) &gt;= 4:                                     │
│                          # add two additional sample points along polyline   │
│                          pts.append((xs[0], ys[0]))                          │
│                          pts.append((xs[len(xs)//2], ys[len(xs)//2]))        │
│                  else:                                                       │
│                      # fallback to bbox center                               │
│                      pts = [( (xmin+xmax)//2, (ymin+ymax)//2 )]              │
│                  m, s = predictor_wrapper.predict_points(pts)                │
│              # m is boolean mask                                             │
│              if isinstance(m, &#x27;np.ndarray&#x27;):                       │
│                  mask = (m.astype(np.uint8) * 255)                           │
│              else:                                                           │
│                  mask = (np.array(m).astype(np.uint8) * 255)                 │
│              score = float(s) if s is not None else None                     │
│              sam_used = True                                                 │
│          except Exception as e:                                              │
│              # SAM failed for this mask; fallback                            │
│              print(f&#x27;Warning: MobileSAM predict failed for mask {i}:    │
│  {e}&#x27;, file=sys.stderr)                                                 │
│              sam_used = False                                                │
│                                                                              │
│      if not sam_used:                                                        │
│          # Rasterize original polygon or box                                 │
│          if parsed_coords[i][0] and parsed_coords[i][1] and                  │
│  len(parsed_coords[i][0])&gt;=3:                                             │
│              mask = rasterize_polygon_to_mask(parsed_coords[i][0],           │
│  parsed_coords[i][1], h, w)                                                  │
│          else:                                                               │
│              mask = rasterize_box_to_mask(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax, h, w)      │
│                                                                              │
│      # Postprocess mask                                                      │
│      mask = clean_mask_keep_largest(mask)                                    │
│      area = int(np.count_nonzero(mask&gt;0))                                 │
│      per_mask_binaries.append(mask)                                          │
│      per_mask_scores.append(score)                                           │
│      per_mask_areas.append(area)                                             │
│      used_sam.append(sam_used)                                               │
│                                                                              │
│      # Optionally save per-mask binary                                       │
│      if args.save_masks:                                                     │
│          outp = os.path.join(masks_dir, f&#x27;mask_{i:04d}.png&#x27;)       │
│          cv2.imwrite(outp, mask)                                             │
│                                                                              │
│  # Build priority order for global overlap resolution                        │
│  n = len(per_mask_binaries)                                                  │
│  indices = list(range(n))                                                    │
│  use_scores = args.use_sam_confidence and all([s is not None for s in        │
│  per_mask_scores])                                                           │
│  if use_scores:                                                              │
│      order = sorted(indices, key=lambda i: (-(per_mask_scores[i] if          │
│  per_mask_scores[i] is not None else -1), -per_mask_areas[i], i))            │
│      print(&#x27;Using SAM confidence to prioritize masks for overlap        │
│  resolution.&#x27;)                                                          │
│  else:                                                                       │
│      order = sorted(indices, key=lambda i: ( -per_mask_areas[i], i))         │
│      if args.use_sam_confidence:                                             │
│          print(&#x27;Warning: --use_sam_confidence was set but not all       │
│  masks have SAM scores; falling back to area-based priority.&#x27;)          │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ </output>                                                                    │

│ finish_reason='stop' content="Sub-task (concise)\n- Implement a lightweight, │
│ dependency-minimal fallback runner /app/run_fallback_minimal.py that         │
│ converts the input CSV masks into non-overlapping polygon masks using only   │
│ libraries available in the current container (numpy and Pillow), so we can   │
│ test the downstream overlap-resolution, postprocessing and CSV output here   │
│ without pandas, cv2, or MobileSAM.\n\nWhy this is the next reasonable small  │
│ step\n- The full pipeline requires packages not present in this container. A │
│ minimal fallback runner exercising rasterization, overlap-resolution,        │
│ largest-CC cleanup, polygon extraction (via a simple border-tracing), and    │
│ CSV writing will let us validate the core non-model logic end-to-end in this │
│ environment and produce concrete outputs for inspection.\n\nHigh-level plan  │
│ outline\n1. CLI\n   - Script accepts: --output_path, --rgb_path, --csv_path  │
│ (all required).\n   - Use Python stdlib argparse.\n\n2. Read CSV without     │
│ pandas\n   - Read the CSV file line-by-line.\n   - Parse header to find      │
│ xmin/xmax/ymin/ymax and coords_x/coords_y column indices.\n   - Parse        │
│ coords_x / coords_y strings using ast.literal_eval or simple comma-split to  │
│ get integer lists.\n\n3. Load image (Pillow) to get width/height.\n\n4.      │
│ Per-mask rasterization (Pillow)\n   - For each row:\n     - If coords define │
│ a polygon: use PIL.ImageDraw.Draw.polygon to draw filled polygon into a      │
│ single-channel uint8 numpy array (0/1).\n     - If only bbox present or      │
│ polygon invalid: rasterize rectangle region.\n   - Store per-mask binary     │
│ masks in a list/array. Optionally save per-mask mask PNGs to                 │
│ output_path/masks/.\n\n5. Per-mask postprocessing\n   - For each binary      │
│ mask:\n     - Remove tiny islands: implement a simple connected-component    │
│ flood-fill (BFS) to identify components; keep the largest component only.\n  │
│ - Fill small holes: a quick approach is to invert the mask within its bbox   │
│ and remove small components in the inverted mask (same BFS).\n     - Compute │
│ mask area (pixel count) and centroid.\n\n6. Global overlap-resolution        │
│ (deterministic)\n   - Order masks by descending area (tie-breaker: original  │
│ index).\n   - Create an integer label canvas (numpy zeros).\n   - Iterate    │
│ masks in priority order, assign pixels where mask==1 and label==0 to that    │
│ mask's label (first-claim wins). This produces a non-overlapping label       │
│ image.\n\n7. Ensure single contiguous mask per label\n   - For each assigned │
│ label, run connected-component flood-fill to find components; keep the       │
│ largest one; any small islands unassigned or reassigned to background.\n\n8. │
│ Polygon extraction (simple border tracing)\n   - For each final binary       │
│ mask:\n     - Extract boundary pixels (pixel has value 1 and at least one    │

│                                                                              │

│ High-level plan outline                                                      │
│                                                                              │
│   1 CLI                                                                      │
│      • Script accepts: --output_path, --rgb_path, --csv_path (all required). │
│      • Use Python stdlib argparse.                                           │
│   2 Read CSV without pandas                                                  │
│      • Read the CSV file line-by-line.                                       │
│      • Parse header to find xmin/xmax/ymin/ymax and coords_x/coords_y column │
│        indices.                                                              │
│      • Parse coords_x / coords_y strings using ast.literal_eval or simple    │

│   3 Load image (Pillow) to get width/height.                                 │

│      • For each row:                                                         │
│         • If coords define a polygon: use PIL.ImageDraw.Draw.polygon to draw │

│      • For each binary mask:                                                 │
│         • Remove tiny islands: implement a simple connected-component        │
│           flood-fill (BFS) to identify components; keep the largest          │
│           component only.                                                    │
│         • Fill small holes: a quick approach is to invert the mask within    │
│           its bbox and remove small components in the inverted mask (same    │
│           BFS).                                                              │
│         • Compute mask area (pixel count) and centroid.                      │

│      • Create an integer label canvas (numpy zeros).                         │
│      • Iterate masks in priority order, assign pixels where mask==1 and      │
│        label==0 to that mask's label (first-claim wins). This produces a     │
│        non-overlapping label image.                                          │
│   7 Ensure single contiguous mask per label                                  │
│      • For each assigned label, run connected-component flood-fill to find   │
│        components; keep the largest one; any small islands unassigned or     │
│        reassigned to background.                                             │
│   8 Polygon extraction (simple border tracing)                               │
│      • For each final binary mask:                                           │
│         • Extract boundary pixels (pixel has value 1 and at least one        │
│           4-neighbor 0).                                                     │
│         • Trace an ordered contour by walking neighbors (Moore-neighbor or   │
│           Bresenham-like) to produce an ordered polyline of (x,y).           │
│         • Simplify the polyline optionally by subsampling or removing        │
│           collinear points.                                                  │
│         • Compute xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax from coordinates.                   │
│   9 CSV writing (stdlib)                                                     │
│      • Write a CSV with same columns as input (preserve other columns        │
│        unchanged) but update xmin,ymin,xmax,ymax and coords_x/coords_y       │
│        (serialize as JSON-like strings).                                     │
│      • Save to <output_path>/converted_metadata.csv.                         │
│  10 Basic validation and outputs                                             │
│                                                                              │
│  • Verify no pairwise bbox overlaps (or at least report any overlapping      │
│    pixels).                                                                  │
│  • Save label overlay PNG (<output_path>/label_overlay.png).                 │
│  • Print a short summary (masks processed, masks saved, any masks that       │
│    became empty, overlap counts).                                            │

│ set([(xmin,ymin),(xmax,ymin),(xmax,ymax),(xmin,ymax)]) pts =                 │

│ --weights_path /path/to/weights.pth --output_path out --rgb_path img.png     │
│ --csv_path metadata.csv\n    python3 convert_masks.py --no_sam --output_path │
│ out --rgb_path img.png --csv_path metadata.csv\n\nThe script is CPU-only and │
│ will not attempt to use CUDA. It will try to load MobileSAM\nif available    │
│ and weights_path provided; on per-mask failure it falls back to              │
│ rasterizing\noriginal polygon/bbox.\n\nOutputs saved to output_path:\n -     │
│ converted_metadata.csv (same columns as input but updated coords and         │
│ bboxes)\n - label_overlay.png (visualization)\n - masks/mask_XXXX.png (if    │
│ --save_masks)\n\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport argparse\nimport    │
│ ast\nimport json\nimport math\nimport traceback\nfrom collections import     │
│ defaultdict\n\n# Imports that are required if available at runtime; keep     │
│ imports local where appropriate\ntry:\n    import numpy as np\n    import    │
│ pandas as pd\n    from PIL import Image\n    import cv2\n    import          │
│ torch\nexcept Exception:\n    # We&#x27;ll handle missing packages at        │
│ runtime; for now allow the script to be imported/compiled\n    pass\n\n\ndef │
│ parse_xy_lists(s):\n    \"\"\"Parse a string representation of a list into a │
│ Python list of numbers.\n    Accepts formats like \"[1, 2, 3]\" or           │
│ \"1,2,3\".\n    \"\"\"\n    if isinstance(s, (list, tuple)):\n        return │
│ list(s)\n    if s is None or (isinstance(s, float) and math.isnan(s)):\n     │
│ return []\n    if not isinstance(s, str):\n        s = str(s)\n    s =       │
│ s.strip()\n    if s == \"\":\n        return []\n    # Try ast.literal_eval  │
│ first\n    try:\n        val = ast.literal_eval(s)\n        if               │
│ isinstance(val, (list, tuple)):\n            return [float(x) for x in       │
│ val]\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    # Fallback: split by commas\n │
│ parts = [p.strip() for p in s.split(&#x27;,&#x27;) if p.strip() !=           │
│ &#x27;&#x27;]\n    out = []\n    for p in parts:\n        try:\n             │
│ out.append(float(p))\n        except Exception:\n            try:\n          │
│ out.append(float(p.strip(&#x27;&#x27;)))\n            except Exception:\n    │
│ pass\n    return out\n\n\ndef ensure_output_dir(path):\n                     │
│ os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)\n\n\ndef load_image_rgb(rgb_path):\n    img │
│ = Image.open(rgb_path).convert(&#x27;RGB&#x27;)\n    arr = np.array(img)\n   │
│ return arr\n\n\ndef is_rectangle_from_coords(x_coords, y_coords, xmin, ymin, │
│ xmax, ymax, tol=1e-3):\n    if len(x_coords) != 4 or len(y_coords) != 4:\n   │
│ return False\n    corners = {(xmin, ymin), (xmax, ymin), (xmax, ymax),       │
│ (xmin, ymax)}\n    pts = set()\n    for x, y in zip(x_coords, y_coords):\n   │
│ pts.add((round(float(x),3), round(float(y),3)))\n    corners_r =             │
│ set((round(float(x),3), round(float(y),3)) for (x,y) in corners)\n    return │
│ pts == corners_r\n\n\ndef rasterize_polygon_to_mask(coords_x, coords_y,      │
│ width, height):\n    # Use cv2.fillPoly; coords_x/y are lists of numbers\n   │
│ mask = np.zeros((height, width), dtype=np.uint8)\n    if len(coords_x) < 3   │
│ or len(coords_y) < 3:\n        return mask\n    pts =                        │
│ np.array([[int(round(x)), int(round(y))] for x,y in zip(coords_x,            │
│ coords_y)], dtype=np.int32)\n    pts = pts.reshape((-1,1,2))\n    try:\n     │
│ cv2.fillPoly(mask, [pts], color=1)\n    except Exception:\n        #         │
│ defensive: clip pts into image and try again\n        pts[:,0,0] =           │
│ np.clip(pts[:,0,0], 0, width-1)\n        pts[:,0,1] = np.clip(pts[:,0,1], 0, │
│ height-1)\n        cv2.fillPoly(mask, [pts], color=1)\n    return            │
│ mask\n\n\ndef rasterize_bbox_to_mask(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax, width,          │
│ height):\n    mask = np.zeros((height, width), dtype=np.uint8)\n    x0 =     │
│ max(0, int(math.floor(xmin)))\n    y0 = max(0, int(math.floor(ymin)))\n      │
│ x1 = min(width-1, int(math.ceil(xmax)))\n    y1 = min(height-1,              │
│ int(math.ceil(ymax)))\n    if x1 >= x0 and y1 >= y0:\n        mask[y0:y1+1,  │
│ x0:x1+1] = 1\n    return mask\n\n\ndef postprocess_mask_keep_largest(mask,   │
│ min_area=10, closing_kernel=3):\n    # mask: binary uint8 (0/1)\n    if      │
│ mask.sum() == 0:\n        return mask\n    # morphological closing to fill   │
│ small holes\n    try:\n        kernel = np.ones((closing_kernel,             │
│ closing_kernel), np.uint8)\n        mask =                                   │
│ cv2.morphologyEx(mask.astype(np.uint8), cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, kernel)\n    except │
│ Exception:\n        pass\n    # connected components to keep largest\n       │
│ num_labels, labels, stats, centroids =                                       │
│ cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(mask.astype(np.uint8), connectivity=8)\n    │
│ if num_labels <= 1:\n        return (mask>0).astype(np.uint8)\n    areas =   │
│ stats[1:, cv2.CC_STAT_AREA]\n    largest_idx = 1 + int(np.argmax(areas))\n   │
│ out = (labels == largest_idx).astype(np.uint8)\n    if out.sum() <           │
│ min_area:\n        # too small: return original largest anyway\n             │
│ return out\n    return out\n\n\ndef mask_to_polygon(mask,                    │
│ epsilon_ratio=0.01):\n    # mask: uint8 binary\n    contours, hierarchy =    │
│ cv2.findContours(mask.astype(np.uint8), cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL,                   │
│ cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)\n    if not contours:\n        return [], []\n    # │
│ pick largest contour by area\n    areas = [cv2.contourArea(c) for c in       │
│ contours]\n    idx = int(np.argmax(areas))\n    cnt = contours[idx]\n    #   │
│ epsilon for approxPolyDP\n    peri = cv2.arcLength(cnt, True)\n    eps =     │
│ max(1.0, epsilon_ratio * peri)\n    approx = cv2.approxPolyDP(cnt, eps,      │
│ True)\n    xs = [int(p[0][0]) for p in approx]\n    ys = [int(p[0][1]) for p │
│ in approx]\n    return xs, ys\n\n\ndef save_mask_png(mask, path):\n    #     │
│ mask: binary uint8\n    im = Image.fromarray((mask255).astype(np.uint8))\n   │
│ im.save(path)\n\n\ndef try_init_mobilesam(weights_path, device):\n           │
│ \"\"\"Attempt multiple known ways to initialize MobileSAM and a predictor    │
│ interface.\n    Returns predictor object with methods set_image(image) and   │
│ predict(...), or raises.\n    The exact MobileSAM APIs differ; this function │
│ tries a few common patterns.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Delay imports to here\n      │
│ import mobile_sam\n    predictor = None\n    model = None\n    # Strategy 1: │
│ MobileSAM class + SamPredictor\n    try:\n        # common interface used in │
│ many wrappers\n        if hasattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;MobileSAM&#x27;):\n      │
│ MobileSAM = mobile_sam.MobileSAM\n            model =                        │
│ MobileSAM(checkpoint=weights_path)\n            # try to find SamPredictor\n │
│ if hasattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;SamPredictor&#x27;):\n                          │
│ SamPredictor = mobile_sam.SamPredictor\n            else:\n                # │
│ sometimes predictor lives in mobile_sam.predictor\n                try:\n    │
│ from mobile_sam.predictor import SamPredictor\n                except        │
│ Exception:\n                    SamPredictor = None\n            if          │
│ SamPredictor is not None:\n                predictor = SamPredictor(model)\n │
│ return predictor, model\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    # Strategy │
│ 2: SamPredictor directly wrapping a model loaded via mobile_sam\n    try:\n  │
│ if hasattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;sam_model_registry&#x27;):\n                    │
│ registry = mobile_sam.sam_model_registry\n            # some registries      │
│ provide build_sam or load_model\n            if hasattr(registry,            │
│ &#x27;load_model&#x27;):\n                model =                            │
│ registry.load_model(weights_path)\n            elif hasattr(registry,        │
│ &#x27;build_sam&#x27;):\n                model =                             │
│ registry.build_sam(checkpoint=weights_path)\n            if model is not     │
│ None:\n                # SamPredictor might be provided\n                if  │
│ hasattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;SamPredictor&#x27;):\n                             │
│ predictor = mobile_sam.SamPredictor(model)\n                else:\n          │
│ try:\n                        from mobile_sam.predictor import               │
│ SamPredictor\n                        predictor = SamPredictor(model)\n      │
│ except Exception:\n                        predictor = None\n                │
│ if predictor is not None:\n                    return predictor, model\n     │
│ except Exception:\n        pass\n    # Strategy 3: fallback - try to import  │
│ SamPredictor from top-level (like original SAM)\n    try:\n        from      │
│ mobile_sam import SamPredictor as SamPredictor2\n        # try to load a     │
│ model via torch.load (if weights_path is a state_dict)\n        model =      │
│ None\n        try:\n            # some package versions expose a function to │
│ build from checkpoint\n            if hasattr(mobile_sam,                    │

│ mobile_sam.build_model(weights_path)\n        except Exception:\n            │

│ model\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n    raise                        │
│ RuntimeError(&#x27;Could not initialize MobileSAM predictor with provided    │
│ mobile_sam package.\\n&#x27;\n                       &#x27;Tried several     │

│ from\\n&#x27;\n                       &#x27;ChaoningZhang/MobileSAM is       │
│ installed and refer to its API for model initialization.&#x27;)\n\n\ndef     │
│ main():\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n                            │

│        • --csv_path (required)                                               │
│        • --no_sam (skip MobileSAM; rasterize originals)                      │
│        • --save_masks (save per-mask PNGs)                                   │
│        • --use_sam_confidence (use SAM confidences to order masks)           │
│        • --run_validator (run validate_masks.py at end)                      │
│        • --verbose                                                           │
│     • Behavior:                                                              │
│        • Loads input CSV (pandas) and RGB image (Pillow → numpy).            │
│        • Parses coords_x / coords_y robustly (handles JSON-like lists and    │
│          comma-separated lists).                                             │
│        • Detects rectangle masks vs polylines and prints counts.             │
│        • Attempts to initialize MobileSAM in CPU mode via a helper that      │
│          tries a few common MobileSAM constructor patterns; logs and falls   │
│          back to rasterization if initialization fails.                      │
│        • For every mask:                                                     │
│           • If SAM available and usable, prompts SAM:                        │
│              • Box prompt for rectangles.                                    │
│              • Point prompt (centroid) for polylines.                        │
│           • If SAM prediction succeeds: converts to binary mask, records     │
│             per-mask area and confidence (if provided).                      │
│           • If SAM fails or not used: rasterizes original polygon/bbox.      │
│           • Postprocesses mask: morphological closing and                    │
│             keep-largest-connected-component (via OpenCV).                   │
│           • Optionally saves per-mask PNGs.                                  │
│        • Global overlap resolution:                                          │
│           • Builds deterministic priority ordering: either by SAM confidence │
│             (if requested and available) or by mask area (descending),       │
│             tie-break by original index.                                     │
│           • Assigns pixels with first-claim-wins into a label image.         │
│           • For each label, keeps only the largest connected component.      │
│        • Converts final masks back to polygons (cv2.findContours +           │
│          approxPolyDP), updates xmin/xmax/ymin/ymax and coords_x/coords_y in │
│          the DataFrame.                                                      │
│        • Adds sam_score and used_sam columns to the output CSV.              │
│        • Saves converted CSV to <output_path>/converted_metadata.csv.        │
│        • Saves a label_overlay.png (tries matplotlib for colored overlay,    │
│          otherwise a grayscale fallback).                                    │
│        • Optionally runs validate_masks.py.                                  │
│                                                                              │
│ Notes about MobileSAM initialization and API assumptions                     │
│                                                                              │
│  • The script tries multiple common ways to build a MobileSAM model and      │
│    predictor, but different MobileSAM releases or forks might have different │
│    APIs.                                                                     │
│  • The helper try_init_mobilesam() attempts various constructor patterns     │
│    used by common wrappers; if none match the installed mobile_sam API, the  │
│    script prints a clear error and falls back to rasterization-only          │
│    behavior.                                                                 │
│  • The predictor usage assumes set_image() and predict(...) methods (typical │
│    SAM-style API). If the installed MobileSAM packaging exposes a different  │
│    predictor interface, small edits may be needed to adapt calls.            │
│  • All torch/model ops are designed to run on CPU (torch.device('cpu')) —    │
│    the script tries to avoid using CUDA.                                     │
│                                                                              │
│ Testing status in this environment                                           │
│                                                                              │
│  • I compiled the script (python -m py_compile) to ensure no syntax errors — │
│    compile succeeded.                                                        │
│  • I did not run the script here because this container lacks critical       │
│    runtime packages (numpy, pandas, Pillow, OpenCV, mobile_sam, torch), so   │
│    execution would fail. The script has fallback (--no_sam) to run in        │

│    numpy/pandas/opencv/Pillow). If you want to test a completely minimal     │
│    no-dependency run, use the helper fallback runner discussion the planner  │
│    proposed (/app/run_fallback_minimal.py), which I did not create here.     │
│  • When run in the proper environment (with the MobileSAM package and        │

│ Limitations, caveats, and recommended next steps                             │
│                                                                              │
│  • Because MobileSAM packaging differs across versions, you should run the   │
│    script in the target environment and verify the predictor initialization. │
│    If model init fails, the script will fallback to rasterization; check     │
│    logs for the exact error and adapt try_init_mobilesam() to the installed  │
│    API if necessary.                                                         │
│  • The SAM prompting is basic: box for rectangles, centroid for polylines.   │
│    If you want higher-quality refinements for polylines, consider sampling a │
│    few points along the polyline and supplying them as point prompts.        │
│  • The script currently uses OpenCV for contouring, morphology, and          │
│    connected components. Ensure opencv-python is installed in the runtime    │

│ def parse_xy_lists(s): """Parse a string representation of a list into a     │
│ Python list of numbers. Accepts formats like "[1, 2, 3]" or "1,2,3". """ if  │
│ isinstance(s, (list, tuple)): return list(s) if s is None or (isinstance(s,  │
│ float) and math.isnan(s)): return [] if not isinstance(s, str): s = str(s) s │
│ = s.strip() if s == "": return [] # Try ast.literal_eval first try: val =    │
│ ast.literal_eval(s) if isinstance(val, (list, tuple)): return [float(x) for  │
│ x in val] except Exception: pass # Fallback: split by commas parts =         │
│ [p.strip() for p in s.split(',') if p.strip() != ''] out = [] for p in       │
│ parts: try: out.append(float(p)) except Exception: try:                      │
│ out.append(float(p.strip(''))) except Exception: pass return out             │
│                                                                              │
│ def ensure_output_dir(path): os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)                │

│ def load_image_rgb(rgb_path): img = Image.open(rgb_path).convert('RGB') arr  │
│ = np.array(img) return arr                                                   │

│ def is_rectangle_from_coords(x_coords, y_coords, xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax,     │
│ tol=1e-3): if len(x_coords) != 4 or len(y_coords) != 4: return False corners │
│ = {(xmin, ymin), (xmax, ymin), (xmax, ymax), (xmin, ymax)} pts = set() for   │
│ x, y in zip(x_coords, y_coords): pts.add((round(float(x),3),                 │
│ round(float(y),3))) corners_r = set((round(float(x),3), round(float(y),3))   │
│ for (x,y) in corners) return pts == corners_r                                │
│                                                                              │
│ def rasterize_polygon_to_mask(coords_x, coords_y, width, height): # Use      │
│ cv2.fillPoly; coords_x/y are lists of numbers mask = np.zeros((height,       │
│ width), dtype=np.uint8) if len(coords_x) < 3 or len(coords_y) < 3: return    │
│ mask pts = np.array([[int(round(x)), int(round(y))] for x,y in zip(coords_x, │
│ coords_y)], dtype=np.int32) pts = pts.reshape((-1,1,2)) try:                 │
│ cv2.fillPoly(mask, [pts], color=1) except Exception: # defensive: clip pts   │
│ into image and try again pts[:,0,0] = np.clip(pts[:,0,0], 0, width-1)        │
│ pts[:,0,1] = np.clip(pts[:,0,1], 0, height-1) cv2.fillPoly(mask, [pts],      │
│ color=1) return mask                                                         │
│                                                                              │
│ def rasterize_bbox_to_mask(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax, width, height): mask =    │
│ np.zeros((height, width), dtype=np.uint8) x0 = max(0, int(math.floor(xmin))) │
│ y0 = max(0, int(math.floor(ymin))) x1 = min(width-1, int(math.ceil(xmax)))   │
│ y1 = min(height-1, int(math.ceil(ymax))) if x1 >= x0 and y1 >= y0:           │
│ mask[y0:y1+1, x0:x1+1] = 1 return mask                                       │
│                                                                              │
│ def postprocess_mask_keep_largest(mask, min_area=10, closing_kernel=3): #    │
│ mask: binary uint8 (0/1) if mask.sum() == 0: return mask # morphological     │
│ closing to fill small holes try: kernel = np.ones((closing_kernel,           │
│ closing_kernel), np.uint8) mask = cv2.morphologyEx(mask.astype(np.uint8),    │
│ cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, kernel) except Exception: pass # connected components to    │
│ keep largest num_labels, labels, stats, centroids =                          │
│ cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(mask.astype(np.uint8), connectivity=8) if   │
│ num_labels <= 1: return (mask>0).astype(np.uint8) areas = stats[1:,          │
│ cv2.CC_STAT_AREA] largest_idx = 1 + int(np.argmax(areas)) out = (labels ==   │
│ largest_idx).astype(np.uint8) if out.sum() < min_area: # too small: return   │
│ original largest anyway return out return out                                │
│                                                                              │
│ def mask_to_polygon(mask, epsilon_ratio=0.01): # mask: uint8 binary          │
│ contours, hierarchy = cv2.findContours(mask.astype(np.uint8),                │
│ cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE) if not contours: return [], [] # │
│ pick largest contour by area areas = [cv2.contourArea(c) for c in contours]  │
│ idx = int(np.argmax(areas)) cnt = contours[idx] # epsilon for approxPolyDP   │
│ peri = cv2.arcLength(cnt, True) eps = max(1.0, epsilon_ratio * peri) approx  │
│ = cv2.approxPolyDP(cnt, eps, True) xs = [int(p[0][0]) for p in approx] ys =  │
│ [int(p[0][1]) for p in approx] return xs, ys                                 │

│ def save_mask_png(mask, path): # mask: binary uint8 im =                     │
│ Image.fromarray((mask*255).astype(np.uint8)) im.save(path)                   │

│ def try_init_mobilesam(weights_path, device): """Attempt multiple known ways │
│ to initialize MobileSAM and a predictor interface. Returns predictor object  │
│ with methods set_image(image) and predict(...), or raises. The exact         │
│ MobileSAM APIs differ; this function tries a few common patterns. """ #      │
│ Delay imports to here import mobile_sam predictor = None model = None #      │
│ Strategy 1: MobileSAM class + SamPredictor try: # common interface used in   │
│ many wrappers if hasattr(mobile_sam, 'MobileSAM'): MobileSAM =               │
│ mobile_sam.MobileSAM model = MobileSAM(checkpoint=weights_path) # try to     │
│ find SamPredictor if hasattr(mobile_sam, 'SamPredictor'): SamPredictor =     │
│ mobile_sam.SamPredictor else: # sometimes predictor lives in                 │
│ mobile_sam.predictor try: from mobile_sam.predictor import SamPredictor      │
│ except Exception: SamPredictor = None if SamPredictor is not None: predictor │
│ = SamPredictor(model) return predictor, model except Exception: pass #       │
│ Strategy 2: SamPredictor directly wrapping a model loaded via mobile_sam     │
│ try: if hasattr(mobile_sam, 'sam_model_registry'): registry =                │
│ mobile_sam.sam_model_registry # some registries provide build_sam or         │
│ load_model if hasattr(registry, 'load_model'): model =                       │
│ registry.load_model(weights_path) elif hasattr(registry, 'build_sam'): model │
│ = registry.build_sam(checkpoint=weights_path) if model is not None: #        │
│ SamPredictor might be provided if hasattr(mobile_sam, 'SamPredictor'):       │
│ predictor = mobile_sam.SamPredictor(model) else: try: from                   │
│ mobile_sam.predictor import SamPredictor predictor = SamPredictor(model)     │
│ except Exception: predictor = None if predictor is not None: return          │
│ predictor, model except Exception: pass # Strategy 3: fallback - try to      │
│ import SamPredictor from top-level (like original SAM) try: from mobile_sam  │
│ import SamPredictor as SamPredictor2 # try to load a model via torch.load    │
│ (if weights_path is a state_dict) model = None try: # some package versions  │
│ expose a function to build from checkpoint if hasattr(mobile_sam,            │
│ 'build_model'): model = mobile_sam.build_model(weights_path) except          │
│ Exception: pass predictor = SamPredictor2(model) return predictor, model     │
│ except Exception: pass </output>                                             │

│       or test the MobileSAM-based path dynamically in this container.        │
│                                                                              │
│ Notes on implementation quality and caveats                                  │
│                                                                              │
│  • The script already includes robust fallback behavior: if MobileSAM is not │
│    initialized or per-mask SAM inference fails, it rasterizes the original   │
│    polygon/bbox and continues downstream processing. This makes it safe to   │
│    run in environments without mobile_sam (use --no_sam to force fallback).  │
│  • try_init_mobilesam tries multiple likely constructor patterns for         │
│    MobileSAM. MobileSAM packages sometimes differ in API; the helper may     │
│    need adjustment to the exact MobileSAM API used in your runtime           │
│    environment (depending on the package version).                           │
│  • Predictor calls assume a predictor.predict(...) interface that may return │
│    (masks, scores) or an object with .masks and .scores. This is handled     │
│    flexibly, but actual MobileSAM versions could have slightly different     │
│    signatures; if the real predictor uses different naming or needs explicit │
│    dtype conversions, small changes might be required.                       │
│  • All torch/model operations in the script are guarded to be CPU-only;      │
│    there is no .cuda() invocation.                                           │
│                                                                              │
│ What I could not do (and why)                                                │
│                                                                              │
│  • I could not exercise the MobileSAM-based refinement end-to-end (run SAM   │
│    predictions) because mobile_sam and torch are not installed in this       │
│    environment. The script is prepared to do so, but dynamic verification    │
│    requires the distilled MobileSAM weights and the package installed in the │
│    environment.                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ What to run to test MobileSAM integration (on a machine with dependencies)   │
│                                                                              │
│  1 Install packages (example, CPU-only torch — adapt for your platform):     │
│     • pip install numpy pillow opencv-python pandas tqdm                     │
│     • Install CPU torch wheel (example):                                     │
│        • pip install --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu torch  │
│          torchvision                                                         │
│     • Install MobileSAM from ChaoningZhang/MobileSAM per that project's      │
│       instructions or pip-install a compatible package (or add the repo to   │
│       PYTHONPATH).                                                           │
│  2 Run the script with weights:                                              │
│     • python3 /app/convert_masks.py --weights_path                           │
│       /path/to/distilled_mobilesam_weights.pth --output_path /path/to/out    │
│       --rgb_path /path/to/img.png --csv_path /path/to/metadata.csv           │
│       --save_masks --use_sam_confidence --run_validator                      │
│     • Or to force fallback-only: python3 /app/convert_masks.py --no_sam      │
│       --output_path /app/out --rgb_path /app/demo_rgb.png --csv_path         │
│       /app/demo_metadata.csv --save_masks --run_validator                    │
│                                                                              │
│ Recommended small follow-ups (if tests show issues)                          │
│                                                                              │
│  • If predictor.predict signature mismatches in the real MobileSAM package,  │
│    adapt predictor calls in convert_masks.py to match exact API (e.g.,       │
│    predictor.predict(box=..., multimask_output=False, return_logits=True) or │
│    predictor.predict_torch(...)).                                            │
│  • If masks are too fragmented or too smoothed, tune morphological           │
│    closing_kernel and min_area in postprocess_mask_keep_largest.             │
│  • If global overlap-resolution choices produce poor assignment, try:        │
│     • Using SAM confidences when available (--use_sam_confidence).           │
│     • Or use an alternative priority (e.g., bounding-box area, interior      │
│       distance map + watershed) in a follow-up step.                         │
│  • If MobileSAM returns masks at a different resolution, ensure              │
│    predictor.set_image(img_arr) is called with the expected image type/shape │
│    before per-mask predict calls.                                            │

│ def parse_xy_lists(s): """Parse a string representation of a list into a     │
│ Python list of numbers. Accepts formats like "[1, 2, 3]" or "1,2,3". """ if  │
│ isinstance(s, (list, tuple)): return list(s) if s is None or (isinstance(s,  │
│ float) and math.isnan(s)): return [] if not isinstance(s, str): s = str(s) s │
│ = s.strip() if s == "": return [] # Try ast.literal_eval first try: val =    │
│ ast.literal_eval(s) if isinstance(val, (list, tuple)): return [float(x) for  │
│ x in val] except Exception: pass # Fallback: split by commas parts =         │
│ [p.strip() for p in s.split(',') if p.strip() != ''] out = [] for p in       │
│ parts: try: out.append(float(p)) except Exception: try:                      │
│ out.append(float(p.strip(''))) except Exception: pass return out             │
│                                                                              │

│ def load_image_rgb(rgb_path): img = Image.open(rgb_path).convert('RGB') arr  │
│ = np.array(img) return arr                                                   │

│ def is_rectangle_from_coords(x_coords, y_coords, xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax,     │
│ tol=1e-3): if len(x_coords) != 4 or len(y_coords) != 4: return False corners │
│ = {(xmin, ymin), (xmax, ymin), (xmax, ymax), (xmin, ymax)} pts = set() for   │
│ x, y in zip(x_coords, y_coords): pts.add((round(float(x),3),                 │
│ round(float(y),3))) corners_r = set((round(float(x),3), round(float(y),3))   │
│ for (x,y) in corners) return pts == corners_r                                │
│                                                                              │
│ def rasterize_polygon_to_mask(coords_x, coords_y, width, height): # Use      │
│ cv2.fillPoly; coords_x/y are lists of numbers mask = np.zeros((height,       │
│ width), dtype=np.uint8) if len(coords_x) < 3 or len(coords_y) < 3: return    │
│ mask pts = np.array([[int(round(x)), int(round(y))] for x,y in zip(coords_x, │
│ coords_y)], dtype=np.int32) pts = pts.reshape((-1,1,2)) try:                 │
│ cv2.fillPoly(mask, [pts], color=1) except Exception: # defensive: clip pts   │
│ into image and try again pts[:,0,0] = np.clip(pts[:,0,0], 0, width-1)        │
│ pts[:,0,1] = np.clip(pts[:,0,1], 0, height-1) cv2.fillPoly(mask, [pts],      │
│ color=1) return mask                                                         │
│                                                                              │
│ def rasterize_bbox_to_mask(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax, width, height): mask =    │
│ np.zeros((height, width), dtype=np.uint8) x0 = max(0, int(math.floor(xmin))) │
│ y0 = max(0, int(math.floor(ymin))) x1 = min(width-1, int(math.ceil(xmax)))   │
│ y1 = min(height-1, int(math.ceil(ymax))) if x1 >= x0 and y1 >= y0:           │
│ mask[y0:y1+1, x0:x1+1] = 1 return mask                                       │
│                                                                              │
│ def postprocess_mask_keep_largest(mask, min_area=10, closing_kernel=3): #    │
│ mask: binary uint8 (0/1) if mask.sum() == 0: return mask # morphological     │
│ closing to fill small holes try: kernel = np.ones((closing_kernel,           │
│ closing_kernel), np.uint8) mask = cv2.morphologyEx(mask.astype(np.uint8),    │
│ cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, kernel) except Exception: pass # connected components to    │
│ keep largest num_labels, labels, stats, centroids =                          │
│ cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(mask.astype(np.uint8), connectivity=8) if   │
│ num_labels <= 1: return (mask>0).astype(np.uint8) areas = stats[1:,          │
│ cv2.CC_STAT_AREA] largest_idx = 1 + int(np.argmax(areas)) out = (labels ==   │
│ largest_idx).astype(np.uint8) if out.sum() < min_area: # too small: return   │
│ original largest anyway return out return out                                │
│                                                                              │
│ def mask_to_polygon(mask, epsilon_ratio=0.01): # mask: uint8 binary          │
│ contours, hierarchy = cv2.findContours(mask.astype(np.uint8),                │
│ cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE) if not contours: return [], [] # │
│ pick largest contour by area areas = [cv2.contourArea(c) for c in contours]  │
│ idx = int(np.argmax(areas)) cnt = contours[idx] # epsilon for approxPolyDP   │
│ peri = cv2.arcLength(cnt, True) eps = max(1.0, epsilon_ratio * peri) approx  │
│ = cv2.approxPolyDP(cnt, eps, True) xs = [int(p[0][0]) for p in approx] ys =  │
│ [int(p[0][1]) for p in approx] return xs, ys                                 │
│                                                                              │
│ def save_mask_png(mask, path): # mask: binary uint8 im =                     │
│ Image.fromarray((mask*255).astype(np.uint8)) im.save(path)                   │

│ def try_init_mobilesam(weights_path, device): """Attempt multiple known ways │
│ to initialize MobileSAM and a predictor interface. Returns predictor object  │
│ with methods set_image(image) and predict(...), or raises. The exact         │
│ MobileSAM APIs differ; this function tries a few common patterns. """ #      │
│ Delay imports to here import mobile_sam predictor = None model = None #      │
│ Strategy 1: MobileSAM class + SamPredictor try: # common interface used in   │
│ many wrappers if hasattr(mobile_sam, 'MobileSAM'): MobileSAM =               │
│ mobile_sam.MobileSAM model = MobileSAM(checkpoint=weights_path) # try to     │
│ find SamPredictor if hasattr(mobile_sam, 'SamPredictor'): SamPredictor =     │
│ mobile_sam.SamPredictor else: # sometimes predictor lives in                 │
│ mobile_sam.predictor try: from mobile_sam.predictor import SamPredictor      │
│ except Exception: SamPredictor = None if SamPredictor is not None: predictor │
│ = SamPredictor(model) return predictor, model except Exception: pass #       │
│ Strategy 2: SamPredictor directly wrapping a model loaded via mobile_sam     │

│ load_model if hasattr(registry, 'load_model'): model =                       │
│ registry.load_model(weights_path) elif hasattr(registry, 'build_sam'): model │
│ = registry.build_sam(checkpoint=weights_path) if model is not None: #        │
│ SamPredictor might be provided if hasattr(mobile_sam, 'SamPredictor'):       │
│ predictor = mobile_sam.SamPredictor(model) else: try: from                   │
│ mobile_sam.predictor import SamPredictor predictor = SamPredictor(model)     │
│ except Exception: predictor = None if predictor is not None: return          │
│ predictor, model except Exception: pass # Strategy 3: fallback - try to      │
│ import SamPredictor from top-level (like original SAM) try: from mobile_sam  │
│ import SamPredictor as SamPredictor2 # try to load a model via torch.load    │
│ (if weights_path is a state_dict) model = None try: # some package versions  │
│ expose a function to build from checkpoint if hasattr(mobile_sam,            │
│ 'build_model'): model = mobile_sam.build_model(weights_path) except          │
│ Exception: pass predictor = SamPredictor2(model) return predictor, model     │
│ except Exception: pass </output>                                             │

│       vertices) and returns N sample points evenly spaced along the polyline │

│        • For target fractions i/(N+1) (or i/(N) depending on choice),        │
│          interpolate along segments to get coordinates.                      │

│        • Use these points as positive point prompts for the SAM predictor    │
│          API (pass them in the expected format).                             │

│          sam_prompt_points with JSON list of points) or log them for         │
│          debugging.                                                          │
│     • For rectangle rows:                                                    │
│        • Keep existing bbox prompt (optionally add center point as an extra  │
│          prompt).                                                            │
│  4 Robustness and fallbacks:                                                 │
│     • If predictor API expects a limited number of point prompts, cap to     │
│       that limit.                                                            │
│     • If predictor throws on multiple point prompts, fallback to centroid    │

│ def parse_xy_lists(s): """Parse a string representation of a list into a     │
│ Python list of numbers. Accepts formats like "[1, 2, 3]" or "1,2,3". """ if  │
│ isinstance(s, (list, tuple)): return list(s) if s is None or (isinstance(s,  │
│ float) and math.isnan(s)): return [] if not isinstance(s, str): s = str(s) s │
│ = s.strip() if s == "": return [] # Try ast.literal_eval first try: val =    │
│ ast.literal_eval(s) if isinstance(val, (list, tuple)): return [float(x) for  │
│ x in val] except Exception: pass # Fallback: split by commas parts =         │
│ [p.strip() for p in s.split(',') if p.strip() != ''] out = [] for p in       │
│ parts: try: out.append(float(p)) except Exception: try:                      │
│ out.append(float(p.strip(''))) except Exception: pass return out             │

│ def is_rectangle_from_coords(x_coords, y_coords, xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax,     │
│ tol=1e-3): if len(x_coords) != 4 or len(y_coords) != 4: return False corners │

│ for (x,y) in corners) return pts == corners_r                                │
│                                                                              │
│ def rasterize_polygon_to_mask(coords_x, coords_y, width, height): # Use      │
│ cv2.fillPoly; coords_x/y are lists of numbers mask = np.zeros((height,       │
│ width), dtype=np.uint8) if len(coords_x) < 3 or len(coords_y) < 3: return    │
│ mask pts = np.array([[int(round(x)), int(round(y))] for x,y in zip(coords_x, │
│ coords_y)], dtype=np.int32) pts = pts.reshape((-1,1,2)) try:                 │
│ cv2.fillPoly(mask, [pts], color=1) except Exception: # defensive: clip pts   │
│ into image and try again pts[:,0,0] = np.clip(pts[:,0,0], 0, width-1)        │
│ pts[:,0,1] = np.clip(pts[:,0,1], 0, height-1) cv2.fillPoly(mask, [pts],      │
│ color=1) return mask                                                         │
│                                                                              │
│ def rasterize_bbox_to_mask(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax, width, height): mask =    │
│ np.zeros((height, width), dtype=np.uint8) x0 = max(0, int(math.floor(xmin))) │
│ y0 = max(0, int(math.floor(ymin))) x1 = min(width-1, int(math.ceil(xmax)))   │
│ y1 = min(height-1, int(math.ceil(ymax))) if x1 >= x0 and y1 >= y0:           │
│ mask[y0:y1+1, x0:x1+1] = 1 return mask                                       │
│                                                                              │
│ def postprocess_mask_keep_largest(mask, min_area=10, closing_kernel=3): #    │
│ mask: binary uint8 (0/1) if mask.sum() == 0: return mask # morphological     │
│ closing to fill small holes try: kernel = np.ones((closing_kernel,           │
│ closing_kernel), np.uint8) mask = cv2.morphologyEx(mask.astype(np.uint8),    │
│ cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, kernel) except Exception: pass # connected components to    │
│ keep largest num_labels, labels, stats, centroids =                          │
│ cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(mask.astype(np.uint8), connectivity=8) if   │
│ num_labels <= 1: return (mask>0).astype(np.uint8) areas = stats[1:,          │
│ cv2.CC_STAT_AREA] largest_idx = 1 + int(np.argmax(areas)) out = (labels ==   │
│ largest_idx).astype(np.uint8) if out.sum() < min_area: # too small: return   │
│ original largest anyway return out return out                                │
│                                                                              │
│ def mask_to_polygon(mask, epsilon_ratio=0.01): # mask: uint8 binary          │
│ contours, hierarchy = cv2.findContours(mask.astype(np.uint8),                │
│ cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE) if not contours: return [], [] # │
│ pick largest contour by area areas = [cv2.contourArea(c) for c in contours]  │
│ idx = int(np.argmax(areas)) cnt = contours[idx] # epsilon for approxPolyDP   │
│ peri = cv2.arcLength(cnt, True) eps = max(1.0, epsilon_ratio * peri) approx  │
│ = cv2.approxPolyDP(cnt, eps, True) xs = [int(p[0][0]) for p in approx] ys =  │
│ [int(p[0][1]) for p in approx] return xs, ys                                 │
│                                                                              │
│ def save_mask_png(mask, path): # mask: binary uint8 im =                     │
│ Image.fromarray((mask*255).astype(np.uint8)) im.save(path)                   │
│                                                                              │
│ def try_init_mobilesam_targeted(weights_path, device, verbose=False):        │
│ """Targeted initializer for ChaoningZhang/MobileSAM packaging. Tries to      │
│ initialize MobileSAM.MobileSAM and the SamPredictor used in that repo.       │
│ Returns (predictor, model). Provides detailed diagnostic messages on         │
│ failure. """ try: import mobile_sam except Exception as e: raise             │
│ RuntimeError('mobile_sam package not importable: ' + str(e))                 │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  # Diagnostic helper                                                         │
│  def _dump(obj):                                                             │
│      try:                                                                    │
│          return &#x27;\n&#x27;.join(sorted([str(x) for x in dir(obj) if not  │
│  x.startswith(&#x27;_&#x27;)])[:200])                                        │
│      except Exception:                                                       │
│          return str(obj)                                                     │
│                                                                              │
│  # Preferred pattern for ChaoningZhang/MobileSAM: mobile_sam.MobileSAM and   │
│  mobile_sam.SamPredictor                                                     │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      if hasattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;MobileSAM&#x27;):                          │
│          if verbose:                                                         │
│              print(&#x27;mobile_sam has MobileSAM class. Attempting          │
│  MobileSAM(checkpoint=...)&#x27;)                                            │
│          MobileSAM = getattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;MobileSAM&#x27;)              │
│          # Instantiate model on CPU                                          │
│          try:                                                                │
│              model = MobileSAM(checkpoint=weights_path,                      │
│  device=&#x27;cpu&#x27;)                                                     │
│          except TypeError:                                                   │
│              # some variants accept (checkpoint) only                        │
│              model = MobileSAM(weights_path)                                 │
│          except Exception as e:                                              │
│              # try without weights then load                                 │
│              try:                                                            │
│                  model = MobileSAM()                                         │
│                  if hasattr(model, &#x27;load_state_dict&#x27;):             │
│                      import torch                                            │
│                      sd = torch.load(weights_path,                           │
│  map_location=&#x27;cpu&#x27;)                                               │
│                      model.load_state_dict(sd)                               │
│              except Exception:                                               │
│                  raise                                                       │
│          # Predictor in that repo is likely mobile_sam.SamPredictor or       │
│  mobile_sam.predictor.SamPredictor                                           │
│          SamPredictor = None                                                 │
│          if hasattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;SamPredictor&#x27;):                   │
│              SamPredictor = getattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;SamPredictor&#x27;)    │
│          else:                                                               │
│              try:                                                            │
│                  from mobile_sam.predictor import SamPredictor               │
│              except Exception:                                               │
│                  SamPredictor = None                                         │
│          if SamPredictor is None:                                            │
│              # try fallback: a class named Predictor                         │
│              if hasattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;Predictor&#x27;):                  │
│                  SamPredictor = getattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;Predictor&#x27;)   │
│          if SamPredictor is None:                                            │
│              raise RuntimeError(&#x27;Could not find SamPredictor in         │
│  mobile_sam package. Available attrs:\n&#x27; + _dump(mobile_sam))           │
│          predictor = SamPredictor(model)                                     │
│          return predictor, model                                             │
│  except Exception as e:                                                      │
│      # provide diagnostic info and continue to other attempts                │
│      last_exc = e                                                            │
│      if verbose:                                                             │
│          print(&#x27;Attempt using mobile_sam.MobileSAM failed:&#x27;,       │
│  repr(e))                                                                    │
│          print(&#x27;mobile_sam dir():\n&#x27;, _dump(mobile_sam))           │
│                                                                              │
│  # Second pattern: some forks expose a registry or build function            │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      if hasattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;sam_model_registry&#x27;):                 │
│          if verbose:                                                         │
│              print(&#x27;Found sam_model_registry; attempting to build/load  │
│  model via registry&#x27;)                                                   │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ </output>                                                                    │

│ def sam_predictor_self_test(predictor, img_arr, verbose=False): """Run a     │
│ small predictor self-test: call set_image and a single small box/prompt      │
│ predict. Returns (True, info) on success, (False, info) on failure. """ info │
│ = {} try: if verbose: print('Running predictor.set_image(...) self-test')    │
│ predictor.set_image(img_arr) except Exception as e: # try passing            │
│ PIL-converted image try: from PIL import Image as PILImage img_pil =         │
│ PILImage.fromarray(img_arr) predictor.set_image(np.array(img_pil)) except    │
│ Exception as e2: info['set_image_error'] = repr(e2) info['predictor_dir'] =  │
│ dir(predictor) return False, info # construct a small center box h, w =      │
│ img_arr.shape[0], img_arr.shape[1] cx0 = max(0, w//2 - 5) cy0 = max(0, h//2  │
│ - 5) cx1 = min(w-1, w//2 + 5) cy1 = min(h-1, h//2 + 5) try: # many           │
│ predictors accept predict(box=..., multimask_output=False) box =             │
│ np.array([cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1], dtype=float) preds = None try: preds =        │
│ predictor.predict(box=box, multimask_output=False) except Exception: try: #  │
│ some predictors use predict(point_coords=..., point_labels=...) pc =         │
│ np.array([[ (cx0+cx1)/2.0, (cy0+cy1)/2.0 ]], dtype=float) pl = np.array([1], │
│ dtype=int) preds = predictor.predict(point_coords=pc, point_labels=pl,       │
│ multimask_output=False) except Exception as e: info['predict_error'] =       │
│ repr(e) info['predictor_dir'] = dir(predictor) return False, info # inspect  │
│ preds info['preds_type'] = type(preds) # attempt to extract masks/scores if  │
│ present masks = None scores = None if isinstance(preds, (tuple, list)): if   │
│ len(preds) >= 1: masks = preds[0] if len(preds) >= 2: scores = preds[1] elif │
│ hasattr(preds, 'masks'): masks = getattr(preds, 'masks') scores =            │
│ getattr(preds, 'scores', None) info['masks_present'] = masks is not None     │
│ info['scores_present'] = scores is not None return True, info except         │
│ Exception as e: info['selftest_exception'] = repr(e) info['predictor_dir'] = │
│ dir(predictor) return False, info                                            │

│ verbose=False):\n    \"\"\"Run a small predictor self-test: call set_image   │

│ return predictor, model\n                else:\n                    try:\n   │
│ from mobile_sam.predictor import SamPredictor\n                              │
│ predictor = SamPredictor(model)\n                        return predictor,   │
│ model\n                    except Exception:\n                        pass\n │
│ except Exception as e:\n        last_exc = e\n        if verbose:\n          │
│ print(&#x27;Registry-based init failed:&#x27;, repr(e))\n\n    # Third       │

│ from mobile_sam.predictor import SamPredictor\n        except Exception:\n   │

│ if available\n            model = None\n            if hasattr(mobile_sam,   │

│ mobile_sam.build_model(weights_path)\n                except Exception:\n    │

│ except Exception:\n                        model = None\n                    │

│ &#x27;Last exception: &#x27; + repr(last_exc) + &#x27;\n&#x27;)\n    raise   │
│ RuntimeError(msg)\n\n\ndef sam_predictor_self_test(predictor, img_arr,       │
│ verbose=False):\n    """Run a small predictor self-test: call set_image and  │
│ a single small box/prompt predict.\n    Returns (True, info) on success,     │
│ (False, info) on failure.\n    """\n    info = {}\n    try:\n        if      │
│ verbose:\n            print(&#x27;Running predictor.set_image(...)           │
│ self-test&#x27;)\n        predictor.set_image(img_arr)\n    except Exception │
│ as e:\n        # try passing PIL-converted image\n        try:\n             │
│ from PIL import Image as PILImage\n            img_pil =                     │
│ PILImage.fromarray(img_arr)\n                                                │
│ predictor.set_image(np.array(img_pil))\n        except Exception as e2:\n    │
│ info[&#x27;set_image_error&#x27;] = repr(e2)\n                               │
│ info[&#x27;predictor_dir&#x27;] = dir(predictor)\n            return False,  │
│ info\n    # construct a small center box\n    h, w = img_arr.shape[0],       │
│ img_arr.shape[1]\n    cx0 = max(0, w//2 - 5)\n    cy0 = max(0, h//2 - 5)\n   │
│ cx1 = min(w-1, w//2 + 5)\n    cy1 = min(h-1, h//2 + 5)\n    try:\n        #  │
│ many predictors accept predict(box=..., multimask_output=False)\n        box │
│ = np.array([cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1], dtype=float)\n        preds = None\n        │
│ try:\n            preds = predictor.predict(box=box,                         │
│ multimask_output=False)\n        except Exception:\n            try:\n       │
│ # some predictors use predict(point_coords=..., point_labels=...)\n          │
│ pc = np.array([[ (cx0+cx1)/2.0, (cy0+cy1)/2.0 ]], dtype=float)\n             │
│ pl = np.array([1], dtype=int)\n                preds =                       │
│ predictor.predict(point_coords=pc, point_labels=pl,                          │
│ multimask_output=False)\n            except Exception as e:\n                │
│ info[&#x27;predict_error&#x27;] = repr(e)\n                                  │
│ info[&#x27;predictor_dir&#x27;] = dir(predictor)\n                return     │
│ False, info\n        # inspect preds\n        info[&#x27;preds_type&#x27;] = │
│ type(preds)\n        # attempt to extract masks/scores if present\n          │
│ masks = None\n        scores = None\n        if isinstance(preds, (tuple,    │
│ list)):\n            if len(preds) >= 1:\n                masks = preds[0]\n │
│ if len(preds) >= 2:\n                scores = preds[1]\n        elif         │
│ hasattr(preds, &#x27;masks&#x27;):\n            masks = getattr(preds,       │
│ &#x27;masks&#x27;)\n            scores = getattr(preds, &#x27;scores&#x27;,  │
│ None)\n        info[&#x27;masks_present&#x27;] = masks is not None\n         │
│ info[&#x27;scores_present&#x27;] = scores is not None\n        return True,  │
│ info\n    except Exception as e:\n                                           │
│ info[&#x27;selftest_exception&#x27;] = repr(e)\n                             │
│ info[&#x27;predictor_dir&#x27;] = dir(predictor)\n        return False,      │
│ info\n\n\ndef main():\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n              │

│ def parse_list_field(s): # Try ast.literal_eval, fallback to comma-split if  │
│ s is None: return [] s = s.strip() if s == "": return [] try: v =            │
│ ast.literal_eval(s) if isinstance(v, (list, tuple)): return                  │
│ [int(round(float(x))) for x in v] except Exception: pass # fallback parts =  │
│ [p for p in s.replace('[','').replace(']','').split(',') if p.strip()!='']   │
│ return [int(round(float(x))) for x in parts]                                 │
│                                                                              │
│ def rasterize_polygon(coords_x, coords_y, width, height): img =              │
│ Image.new('L', (width, height), 0) draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img) pts =          │
│ list(zip(coords_x, coords_y)) if len(pts) >= 3: try: draw.polygon(pts,       │
│ outline=1, fill=1) except Exception: # maybe coordinates out of bounds or    │
│ invalid pass return np.array(img, dtype=np.uint8)                            │
│                                                                              │
│ def bbox_to_mask(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax, width, height): img =               │
│ Image.new('L', (width, height), 0) draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img) # ensure ints  │
│ and clipped xmin = max(0, int(round(xmin))) ymin = max(0, int(round(ymin)))  │
│ xmax = min(width-1, int(round(xmax))) ymax = min(height-1, int(round(ymax))) │
│ if xmax >= xmin and ymax >= ymin: draw.rectangle([xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax],   │
│ outline=1, fill=1) return np.array(img, dtype=np.uint8)                      │
│                                                                              │
│ def largest_connected_component(mask): # mask is 2D uint8 with 0/1 h, w =    │
│ mask.shape visited = np.zeros_like(mask, dtype=np.uint8) best_label = None   │
│ best_size = 0 best_coords = None dirs = [(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)] for y in │
│ range(h): for x in range(w): if mask[y,x] and not visited[y,x]: # BFS stack  │
│ = [(x,y)] visited[y,x]=1 comp = [(x,y)] while stack: cx, cy = stack.pop()    │
│ for dx,dy in dirs: nx, ny = cx+dx, cy+dy if 0 <= nx < w and 0 <= ny < h and  │
│ mask[ny,nx] and not visited[ny,nx]: visited[ny,nx]=1 stack.append((nx,ny))   │
│ comp.append((nx,ny)) if len(comp) > best_size: best_size = len(comp)         │
│ best_coords = comp newmask = np.zeros_like(mask, dtype=np.uint8) if          │
│ best_coords: for (x,y) in best_coords: newmask[y,x]=1 return newmask,        │
│ best_size                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│ def fill_holes(mask): # fill holes by marking background connected to        │
│ border, then fill other background h,w = mask.shape inv =                    │
│ (mask==0).astype(np.uint8) visited = np.zeros_like(inv) from collections     │
│ import deque q = deque() # add border background pixels for x in range(w):   │
│ if inv[0,x] and not visited[0,x]: visited[0,x]=1; q.append((x,0)) if         │
│ inv[h-1,x] and not visited[h-1,x]: visited[h-1,x]=1; q.append((x,h-1)) for y │
│ in range(h): if inv[y,0] and not visited[y,0]: visited[y,0]=1;               │
│ q.append((0,y)) if inv[y,w-1] and not visited[y,w-1]: visited[y,w-1]=1;      │
│ q.append((w-1,y)) dirs = [(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)] while q: x,y =          │
│ q.popleft() for dx,dy in dirs: nx, ny = x+dx, y+dy if 0 <= nx < w and 0 <=   │
│ ny < h and inv[ny,nx] and not visited[ny,nx]: visited[ny,nx]=1;              │
│ q.append((nx,ny)) # visited marks external background; holes are inv==1 and  │
│ visited==0 holes = (inv==1) & (visited==0) out = mask.copy() out[holes]=1    │
│ return out                                                                   │
│                                                                              │
│ def extract_boundary_sorted(mask): # mask: 0/1 ys, xs = np.nonzero(mask) if  │
│ len(xs)==0: return [],[] # boundary points: a pixel that has at least one    │
│ 4-neighbor 0 h,w = mask.shape boundary = [] for x,y in zip(xs,ys):           │
│ is_boundary = False for dx,dy in [(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)]: nx, ny = x+dx, │
│ y+dy if nx <0 or nx>=w or ny<0 or ny>=h or mask[ny,nx]==0: is_boundary =     │
│ True; break if is_boundary: boundary.append((x,y)) if len(boundary)==0: #    │
│ fallback to all pixels boundary = list(zip(xs,ys)) # compute centroid cx =   │
│ sum(p[0] for p in boundary)/len(boundary) cy = sum(p[1] for p in             │
│ boundary)/len(boundary) # sort by angle pts = sorted(boundary, key=lambda p: │
│ math.atan2(p[1]-cy, p[0]-cx)) xs_sorted = [int(p[0]) for p in pts] ys_sorted │
│ = [int(p[1]) for p in pts] # simplify: remove consecutive collinear def      │
│ simplify(xs, ys): if len(xs) <= 2: return xs, ys sx=[xs[0]]; sy=[ys[0]] for  │
│ i in range(1,len(xs)): x0,y0 = sx[-1], sy[-1] x1,y1 = xs[i], ys[i] if        │
│ len(sx)>=2: x_prev, y_prev = sx[-2], sy[-2] # check collinearity of          │
│ prev->last->current if (x0-x_prev)(y1-y0) == (y0-y_prev)(x1-x0): #           │
│ collinear: replace last sx[-1]=x1; sy[-1]=y1 continue sx.append(x1);         │
│ sy.append(y1) return sx, sy xs_s, ys_s = simplify(xs_sorted, ys_sorted)      │
│ return xs_s, ys_s                                                            │

│ finish_reason='stop' content='Sub-task (concise)\n- Implement a              │
│ post-assignment overlap-resolution pass that takes the current labeled image │
│ (after "first-claim wins") and deterministically reassigns                   │
│ overlapping/contested pixels so that no pixels remain shared and each final  │
│ label is contiguous. Priority: use SAM confidence when available; otherwise  │
│ resolve by local adjacency majority (pixels go to the neighboring label with │
│ the largest shared border) and finally fall back to area. Save updated label │
│ map, update polygons/CSV, and write before/after debug overlays.\n\nWhy this │
│ is the next reasonable small step\n- The pipeline already produces per-mask  │
│ binary masks and a deterministic first-claim label map, but the minimal      │
│ validator found residual overlaps (two mask pairs). A localized reassignment │
│ pass is the next small, focused improvement that will remove remaining       │
│ overlaps while preserving mask integrity and contiguity. It does not require │
│ SAM or model changes and operates only on the raster label image produced    │
│ earlier.\n\nHigh-level plan outline\n1. Inputs\n   - Load the current label  │
│ image (integer labels) produced by convert_masks.py or the fallback          │
│ runner.\n   - Load per-mask metadata (DataFrame / CSV) including per-mask    │
│ area and optional sam_score column.\n   - Load image dimensions.\n\n2.       │
│ Identify contested pixels / overlap regions\n   - Compute pixels where more  │
│ than one mask claimed the pixel originally (you may have an overlap mask if  │
│ you kept it; otherwise recompute by summing per-mask binaries to find pixels │
│ with sum>1).\n   - Extract connected components of the contested pixel set   │
│ to operate on localized regions.\n\n3. Resolve each contested region         │
│ deterministically\n   For each contested connected region:\n   - Gather      │
│ candidate labels adjacent to that region (labels that border the contested   │
│ pixels).\n   - For each candidate label compute:\n     - If sam_score exists │
│ for all candidates and --use_sam_confidence is True: use sam_score to rank   │
│ candidates (highest score wins for the whole region).\n     - Else compute   │
│ adjacency metric: count number of neighboring pixels (shared border length)  │
│ between the contested region and each candidate label.\n     - As fallback,  │
│ use candidate mask area (larger area preferred).\n   - Assign the entire     │
│ contested region (or assign pixel-wise by nearest-adjacent label in case of  │
│ ties/heterogeneous adjacency) to the chosen winner label.\n   - (Optional    │
│ refinement) For large contested regions where adjacency is mixed, assign     │
│ per-pixel to nearest candidate label using distance transform to each        │
│ candidate mask (pixel-wise Voronoi) to avoid arbitrary whole-region          │
│ assignment.\n\n4. Post-resolution cleanup\n   - After all contested regions  │
│ processed:\n     - For each label, recompute connected components and keep   │
│ the largest connected component; for small orphan islands that were          │
│ disconnected, reassign those pixels to the neighboring label with the        │
│ largest adjacent border.\n     - Recompute areas and optionally SAM          │
│ confidences remain unchanged.\n   - Ensure no pixel is assigned to more than │
│ one label and no pixel remains unassigned (assign remaining background       │
