╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭────────────────────────── subtaskplanner - message ──────────────────────────╮
│ Sub-task (concise)                                                           │
│                                                                              │
│  • Implement a post-assignment overlap-resolution pass that takes the        │
│    current labeled image (after "first-claim wins") and deterministically    │
│    reassigns overlapping/contested pixels so that no pixels remain shared    │
│    and each final label is contiguous. Priority: use SAM confidence when     │
│    available; otherwise resolve by local adjacency majority (pixels go to    │
│    the neighboring label with the largest shared border) and finally fall    │
│    back to area. Save updated label map, update polygons/CSV, and write      │
│    before/after debug overlays.                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ Why this is the next reasonable small step                                   │
│                                                                              │
│  • The pipeline already produces per-mask binary masks and a deterministic   │
│    first-claim label map, but the minimal validator found residual overlaps  │
│    (two mask pairs). A localized reassignment pass is the next small,        │
│    focused improvement that will remove remaining overlaps while preserving  │
│    mask integrity and contiguity. It does not require SAM or model changes   │
│    and operates only on the raster label image produced earlier.             │
│                                                                              │
│ High-level plan outline                                                      │
│                                                                              │
│  1 Inputs                                                                    │
│     • Load the current label image (integer labels) produced by              │
│       convert_masks.py or the fallback runner.                               │
│     • Load per-mask metadata (DataFrame / CSV) including per-mask area and   │
│       optional sam_score column.                                             │
│     • Load image dimensions.                                                 │
│  2 Identify contested pixels / overlap regions                               │
│     • Compute pixels where more than one mask claimed the pixel originally   │
│       (you may have an overlap mask if you kept it; otherwise recompute by   │
│       summing per-mask binaries to find pixels with sum>1).                  │
│     • Extract connected components of the contested pixel set to operate on  │
│       localized regions.                                                     │
│  3 Resolve each contested region deterministically For each contested        │
│    connected region:                                                         │
│     • Gather candidate labels adjacent to that region (labels that border    │
│       the contested pixels).                                                 │
│     • For each candidate label compute:                                      │
│        • If sam_score exists for all candidates and --use_sam_confidence is  │
│          True: use sam_score to rank candidates (highest score wins for the  │
│          whole region).                                                      │
│        • Else compute adjacency metric: count number of neighboring pixels   │
│          (shared border length) between the contested region and each        │
│          candidate label.                                                    │
│        • As fallback, use candidate mask area (larger area preferred).       │
│     • Assign the entire contested region (or assign pixel-wise by            │
│       nearest-adjacent label in case of ties/heterogeneous adjacency) to the │
│       chosen winner label.                                                   │
│     • (Optional refinement) For large contested regions where adjacency is   │
│       mixed, assign per-pixel to nearest candidate label using distance      │
│       transform to each candidate mask (pixel-wise Voronoi) to avoid         │
│       arbitrary whole-region assignment.                                     │
│  4 Post-resolution cleanup                                                   │
│     • After all contested regions processed:                                 │
│        • For each label, recompute connected components and keep the largest │
│          connected component; for small orphan islands that were             │
│          disconnected, reassign those pixels to the neighboring label with   │
│          the largest adjacent border.                                        │
│        • Recompute areas and optionally SAM confidences remain unchanged.    │
│     • Ensure no pixel is assigned to more than one label and no pixel        │
│       remains unassigned (assign remaining background pixels to 0).          │
│  5 Convert labels back to polygons and CSV                                   │
│     • Extract contours for each final label (cv2.findContours or fallback    │
│       raster-to-contour).                                                    │
│     • Update xmin,ymin,xmax,ymax and coords_x/coords_y in the CSV for each   │
│       original row (preserve row order).                                     │
│     • Save updated CSV to <output_path>/converted_metadata_resolved.csv (or  │
│       overwrite converted_metadata.csv if preferred).                        │
│  6 Debug outputs & logging                                                   │
│     • Save overlay images:                                                   │
│        • Before resolution: <output_path>/label_overlay_before.png (if not   │
│          already present).                                                   │
│        • After resolution: <output_path>/label_overlay_after.png.            │
│        • Highlight originally contested regions in a red overlay for         │
│          inspection.                                                         │
│     • Log per-contested-region decisions (region id, pixel count, candidate  │
│       labels, chosen label, reason: sam_score/adjacency/area).               │
│  7 Validation                                                                │
│     • Run the minimal validator (validate_masks_minimal.py) on the updated   │
│       CSV and include its report.                                            │
│     • If any validation still fails, record failing rows and top issues.     │

│ def parse_xy_lists(s): """Parse a string representation of a list into a     │
│ Python list of numbers. Accepts formats like "[1, 2, 3]" or "1,2,3". """ if  │
│ isinstance(s, (list, tuple)): return list(s) if s is None or (isinstance(s,  │
│ float) and math.isnan(s)): return [] if not isinstance(s, str): s = str(s) s │
│ = s.strip() if s == "": return [] # Try ast.literal_eval first try: val =    │
│ ast.literal_eval(s) if isinstance(val, (list, tuple)): return [float(x) for  │
│ x in val] except Exception: pass # Fallback: split by commas parts =         │
│ [p.strip() for p in s.split(',') if p.strip() != ''] out = [] for p in       │
│ parts: try: out.append(float(p)) except Exception: try:                      │
│ out.append(float(p.strip(''))) except Exception: pass return out             │

│ def is_rectangle_from_coords(x_coords, y_coords, xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax,     │
│ tol=1e-3): if len(x_coords) != 4 or len(y_coords) != 4: return False corners │

│ round(float(y),3))) corners_r = set((round(float(x),3), round(float(y),3))   │
│ for (x,y) in corners) return pts == corners_r                                │

│ def rasterize_polygon_to_mask(coords_x, coords_y, width, height): # Use      │
│ cv2.fillPoly; coords_x/y are lists of numbers mask = np.zeros((height,       │
│ width), dtype=np.uint8) if len(coords_x) < 3 or len(coords_y) < 3: return    │
│ mask pts = np.array([[int(round(x)), int(round(y))] for x,y in zip(coords_x, │
│ coords_y)], dtype=np.int32) pts = pts.reshape((-1,1,2)) try:                 │
│ cv2.fillPoly(mask, [pts], color=1) except Exception: # defensive: clip pts   │
│ into image and try again pts[:,0,0] = np.clip(pts[:,0,0], 0, width-1)        │
│ pts[:,0,1] = np.clip(pts[:,0,1], 0, height-1) cv2.fillPoly(mask, [pts],      │
│ color=1) return mask                                                         │

│ def rasterize_bbox_to_mask(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax, width, height): mask =    │
│ np.zeros((height, width), dtype=np.uint8) x0 = max(0, int(math.floor(xmin))) │
│ y0 = max(0, int(math.floor(ymin))) x1 = min(width-1, int(math.ceil(xmax)))   │
│ y1 = min(height-1, int(math.ceil(ymax))) if x1 >= x0 and y1 >= y0:           │
│ mask[y0:y1+1, x0:x1+1] = 1 return mask                                       │

│ def postprocess_mask_keep_largest(mask, min_area=10, closing_kernel=3): #    │
│ mask: binary uint8 (0/1) if mask.sum() == 0: return mask # morphological     │
│ closing to fill small holes try: kernel = np.ones((closing_kernel,           │
│ closing_kernel), np.uint8) mask = cv2.morphologyEx(mask.astype(np.uint8),    │
│ cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, kernel) except Exception: pass # connected components to    │
│ keep largest num_labels, labels, stats, centroids =                          │
│ cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(mask.astype(np.uint8), connectivity=8) if   │
│ num_labels <= 1: return (mask>0).astype(np.uint8) areas = stats[1:,          │
│ cv2.CC_STAT_AREA] largest_idx = 1 + int(np.argmax(areas)) out = (labels ==   │
│ largest_idx).astype(np.uint8) if out.sum() < min_area: # too small: return   │
│ original largest anyway return out return out                                │

│ def mask_to_polygon(mask, epsilon_ratio=0.01): # mask: uint8 binary          │
│ contours, hierarchy = cv2.findContours(mask.astype(np.uint8),                │
│ cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE) if not contours: return [], [] # │
│ pick largest contour by area areas = [cv2.contourArea(c) for c in contours]  │
│ idx = int(np.argmax(areas)) cnt = contours[idx] # epsilon for approxPolyDP   │
│ peri = cv2.arcLength(cnt, True) eps = max(1.0, epsilon_ratio * peri) approx  │
│ = cv2.approxPolyDP(cnt, eps, True) xs = [int(p[0][0]) for p in approx] ys =  │
│ [int(p[0][1]) for p in approx] return xs, ys                                 │

│ def sample_points_along_polyline(xs, ys, num_points, width, height):         │
│ """Sample num_points evenly along the polyline defined by xs, ys. Returns    │
│ list of (x,y) floats clamped to image bounds. """ pts = [(float(x),          │
│ float(y)) for x,y in zip(xs, ys)] if len(pts) == 0 or num_points <= 0:       │
│ return [] # compute segment lengths seg_lens = [] for i in                   │
│ range(len(pts)-1): x0,y0 = pts[i] x1,y1 = pts[i+1]                           │
│ seg_lens.append(math.hypot(x1-x0, y1-y0)) total = sum(seg_lens) if total ==  │
│ 0: # degenerate: return centroid repeated or unique point cx = sum(p[0] for  │
│ p in pts)/len(pts) cy = sum(p[1] for p in pts)/len(pts) return               │
│ [[min(max(cx,0), width-1), min(max(cy,0), height-1)] for _ in                │
│ range(num_points)] cum = [0] for l in seg_lens: cum.append(cum[-1]+l) out =  │
│ [] # sample at fractions (i+1)/(num_points+1) for k in range(num_points):    │
│ target = (k+1) * total / (num_points+1) # find segment for si in             │
│ range(len(seg_lens)): if cum[si] <= target <= cum[si+1] or si ==             │
│ len(seg_lens)-1: t = (target - cum[si]) / (seg_lens[si] if seg_lens[si]>0    │
│ else 1.0) x0,y0 = pts[si] x1,y1 = pts[si+1] xi = x0 + t*(x1-x0) yi = y0 +    │
│ t*(y1-y0) xi = min(max(xi, 0.0), width-1.0) yi = min(max(yi, 0.0),           │
│ height-1.0) out.append([xi, yi]) break return out                            │

│ def sam_predictor_self_test(predictor, img_arr, verbose=False): """Run a     │
│ small predictor self-test: call set_image and a single small box/prompt      │
│ predict. Returns (True, info) on success, (False, info) on failure. """ info │
│ = {} try: if verbose: print('Running predictor.set_image(...) self-test')    │
│ predictor.set_image(img_arr) except Exception as e: # try passing            │
│ PIL-converted image try: from PIL import Image as PILImage img_pil =         │
│ PILImage.fromarray(img_arr) predictor.set_image(np.array(img_pil)) except    │
│ Exception as e2: info['set_image_error'] = repr(e2) info['predictor_dir'] =  │
│ dir(predictor) return False, info # construct a small center box h, w =      │
│ img_arr.shape[0], img_arr.shape[1] cx0 = max(0, w//2 - 5) cy0 = max(0, h//2  │
│ - 5) cx1 = min(w-1, w//2 + 5) cy1 = min(h-1, h//2 + 5) try: # many           │
│ predictors accept predict(box=..., multimask_output=False) box =             │
│ np.array([cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1], dtype=float) preds = None try: preds =        │
│ predictor.predict(box=box, multimask_output=False) except Exception: try: #  │
│ some predictors use predict(point_coords=..., point_labels=...) pc =         │
│ np.array([[ (cx0+cx1)/2.0, (cy0+cy1)/2.0 ]], dtype=float) pl = np.array([1], │
│ dtype=int) preds = predictor.predict(point_coords=pc, point_labels=pl,       │
│ multimask_output=False) except Exception as e: info['predict_error'] =       │
│ repr(e) info['predictor_dir'] = dir(predictor) return False, info # inspect  │
│ preds info['preds_type'] = type(preds) # attempt to extract masks/scores if  │
│ present masks = None scores = None if isinstance(preds, (tuple, list)): if   │
│ len(preds) >= 1: masks = preds[0] if len(preds) >= 2: scores = preds[1] elif │
│ hasattr(preds, 'masks'): masks = getattr(preds, 'masks') scores =            │
│ getattr(preds, 'scores', None) info['masks_present'] = masks is not None     │
│ info['scores_present'] = scores is not None return True, info except         │
│ Exception as e: info['selftest_exception'] = repr(e) info['predictor_dir'] = │
│ dir(predictor) return False, info                                            │

│ def parse_list_field(s): # Try ast.literal_eval, fallback to comma-split if  │

│ def rasterize_polygon(coords_x, coords_y, width, height): img =              │
│ Image.new('L', (width, height), 0) draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img) pts =          │
│ list(zip(coords_x, coords_y)) if len(pts) >= 3: try: draw.polygon(pts,       │

│ def bbox_to_mask(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax, width, height): img =               │
│ Image.new('L', (width, height), 0) draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img) # ensure ints  │
│ and clipped xmin = max(0, int(round(xmin))) ymin = max(0, int(round(ymin)))  │

│ def largest_connected_component(mask): # mask is 2D uint8 with 0/1 h, w =    │
│ mask.shape visited = np.zeros_like(mask, dtype=np.uint8) best_label = None   │
│ best_size = 0 best_coords = None dirs = [(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)] for y in │
│ range(h): for x in range(w): if mask[y,x] and not visited[y,x]: # BFS stack  │
│ = [(x,y)] visited[y,x]=1 comp = [(x,y)] while stack: cx, cy = stack.pop()    │
│ for dx,dy in dirs: nx, ny = cx+dx, cy+dy if 0 <= nx < w and 0 <= ny < h and  │
│ mask[ny,nx] and not visited[ny,nx]: visited[ny,nx]=1 stack.append((nx,ny))   │
│ comp.append((nx,ny)) if len(comp) > best_size: best_size = len(comp)         │
│ best_coords = comp newmask = np.zeros_like(mask, dtype=np.uint8) if          │
│ best_coords: for (x,y) in best_coords: newmask[y,x]=1 return newmask,        │
│ best_size                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│ def fill_holes(mask): # fill holes by marking background connected to        │
│ border, then fill other background h,w = mask.shape inv =                    │
│ (mask==0).astype(np.uint8) visited = np.zeros_like(inv) from collections     │
│ import deque q = deque() # add border background pixels for x in range(w):   │
│ if inv[0,x] and not visited[0,x]: visited[0,x]=1; q.append((x,0)) if         │
│ inv[h-1,x] and not visited[h-1,x]: visited[h-1,x]=1; q.append((x,h-1)) for y │
│ in range(h): if inv[y,0] and not visited[y,0]: visited[y,0]=1;               │
│ q.append((0,y)) if inv[y,w-1] and not visited[y,w-1]: visited[y,w-1]=1;      │
│ q.append((w-1,y)) dirs = [(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)] while q: x,y =          │
│ q.popleft() for dx,dy in dirs: nx, ny = x+dx, y+dy if 0 <= nx < w and 0 <=   │
│ ny < h and inv[ny,nx] and not visited[ny,nx]: visited[ny,nx]=1;              │
│ q.append((nx,ny)) # visited marks external background; holes are inv==1 and  │
│ visited==0 holes = (inv==1) & (visited==0) out = mask.copy() out[holes]=1    │
│ return out                                                                   │

│ def extract_boundary_sorted(mask): # mask: 0/1 ys, xs = np.nonzero(mask) if  │
│ len(xs)==0: return [],[] # boundary points: a pixel that has at least one    │
│ 4-neighbor 0 h,w = mask.shape boundary = [] for x,y in zip(xs,ys):           │
│ is_boundary = False for dx,dy in [(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)]: nx, ny = x+dx, │
│ y+dy if nx <0 or nx>=w or ny<0 or ny>=h or mask[ny,nx]==0: is_boundary =     │
│ True; break if is_boundary: boundary.append((x,y)) if len(boundary)==0: #    │
│ fallback to all pixels boundary = list(zip(xs,ys)) # compute centroid cx =   │
│ sum(p[0] for p in boundary)/len(boundary) cy = sum(p[1] for p in             │
│ boundary)/len(boundary) # sort by angle pts = sorted(boundary, key=lambda p: │
│ math.atan2(p[1]-cy, p[0]-cx)) xs_sorted = [int(p[0]) for p in pts] ys_sorted │
│ = [int(p[1]) for p in pts] # simplify: remove consecutive collinear def      │
│ simplify(xs, ys): if len(xs) <= 2: return xs, ys sx=[xs[0]]; sy=[ys[0]] for  │
│ i in range(1,len(xs)): x0,y0 = sx[-1], sy[-1] x1,y1 = xs[i], ys[i] if        │
│ len(sx)>=2: x_prev, y_prev = sx[-2], sy[-2] # check collinearity of          │
│ prev->last->current if (x0-x_prev)(y1-y0) == (y0-y_prev)(x1-x0): #           │
│ collinear: replace last sx[-1]=x1; sy[-1]=y1 continue sx.append(x1);         │
│ sy.append(y1) return sx, sy xs_s, ys_s = simplify(xs_sorted, ys_sorted)      │
│ return xs_s, ys_s                                                            │

│ x in val] except Exception: pass # Fallback: split by commas parts =         │
│ [p.strip() for p in s.split(',') if p.strip() != ''] out = [] for p in       │
│ parts: try: out.append(float(p)) except Exception: try:                      │
│ out.append(float(p.strip(''))) except Exception: pass return out             │
│                                                                              │
│ def ensure_output_dir(path): os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)                │
│                                                                              │
│ def load_image_rgb(rgb_path): img = Image.open(rgb_path).convert('RGB') arr  │
│ = np.array(img) return arr                                                   │

│ def is_rectangle_from_coords(x_coords, y_coords, xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax,     │
│ tol=1e-3): if len(x_coords) != 4 or len(y_coords) != 4: return False corners │
│ = {(xmin, ymin), (xmax, ymin), (xmax, ymax), (xmin, ymax)} pts = set() for   │
│ x, y in zip(x_coords, y_coords): pts.add((round(float(x),3),                 │
│ round(float(y),3))) corners_r = set((round(float(x),3), round(float(y),3))   │
│ for (x,y) in corners) return pts == corners_r                                │
│                                                                              │
│ def rasterize_polygon_to_mask(coords_x, coords_y, width, height): # Use      │
│ cv2.fillPoly; coords_x/y are lists of numbers mask = np.zeros((height,       │
│ width), dtype=np.uint8) if len(coords_x) < 3 or len(coords_y) < 3: return    │
│ mask pts = np.array([[int(round(x)), int(round(y))] for x,y in zip(coords_x, │
│ coords_y)], dtype=np.int32) pts = pts.reshape((-1,1,2)) try:                 │
│ cv2.fillPoly(mask, [pts], color=1) except Exception: # defensive: clip pts   │
│ into image and try again pts[:,0,0] = np.clip(pts[:,0,0], 0, width-1)        │
│ pts[:,0,1] = np.clip(pts[:,0,1], 0, height-1) cv2.fillPoly(mask, [pts],      │
│ color=1) return mask                                                         │
│                                                                              │
│ def rasterize_bbox_to_mask(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax, width, height): mask =    │
│ np.zeros((height, width), dtype=np.uint8) x0 = max(0, int(math.floor(xmin))) │
│ y0 = max(0, int(math.floor(ymin))) x1 = min(width-1, int(math.ceil(xmax)))   │
│ y1 = min(height-1, int(math.ceil(ymax))) if x1 >= x0 and y1 >= y0:           │
│ mask[y0:y1+1, x0:x1+1] = 1 return mask                                       │
│                                                                              │
│ def postprocess_mask_keep_largest(mask, min_area=10, closing_kernel=3): #    │
│ mask: binary uint8 (0/1) if mask.sum() == 0: return mask # morphological     │
│ closing to fill small holes try: kernel = np.ones((closing_kernel,           │
│ closing_kernel), np.uint8) mask = cv2.morphologyEx(mask.astype(np.uint8),    │
│ cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, kernel) except Exception: pass # connected components to    │
│ keep largest num_labels, labels, stats, centroids =                          │
│ cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(mask.astype(np.uint8), connectivity=8) if   │
│ num_labels <= 1: return (mask>0).astype(np.uint8) areas = stats[1:,          │
│ cv2.CC_STAT_AREA] largest_idx = 1 + int(np.argmax(areas)) out = (labels ==   │
│ largest_idx).astype(np.uint8) if out.sum() < min_area: # too small: return   │
│ original largest anyway return out return out                                │
│                                                                              │
│ def mask_to_polygon(mask, epsilon_ratio=0.01): # mask: uint8 binary          │
│ contours, hierarchy = cv2.findContours(mask.astype(np.uint8),                │
│ cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE) if not contours: return [], [] # │
│ pick largest contour by area areas = [cv2.contourArea(c) for c in contours]  │
│ idx = int(np.argmax(areas)) cnt = contours[idx] # epsilon for approxPolyDP   │
│ peri = cv2.arcLength(cnt, True) eps = max(1.0, epsilon_ratio * peri) approx  │
│ = cv2.approxPolyDP(cnt, eps, True) xs = [int(p[0][0]) for p in approx] ys =  │
│ [int(p[0][1]) for p in approx] return xs, ys                                 │
│                                                                              │
│ def save_mask_png(mask, path): # mask: binary uint8 im =                     │
│ Image.fromarray((mask*255).astype(np.uint8)) im.save(path)                   │
│                                                                              │
│ def sample_points_along_polyline(xs, ys, num_points, width, height):         │
│ """Sample num_points evenly along the polyline defined by xs, ys. Returns    │
│ list of (x,y) floats clamped to image bounds. """ pts = [(float(x),          │
│ float(y)) for x,y in zip(xs, ys)] if len(pts) == 0 or num_points <= 0:       │
│ return [] # compute segment lengths seg_lens = [] for i in                   │
│ range(len(pts)-1): x0,y0 = pts[i] x1,y1 = pts[i+1]                           │
│ seg_lens.append(math.hypot(x1-x0, y1-y0)) total = sum(seg_lens) if total ==  │
│ 0: # degenerate: return centroid repeated or unique point cx = sum(p[0] for  │
│ p in pts)/len(pts) cy = sum(p[1] for p in pts)/len(pts) return               │
│ [[min(max(cx,0), width-1), min(max(cy,0), height-1)] for _ in                │
│ range(num_points)] cum = [0] for l in seg_lens: cum.append(cum[-1]+l) out =  │
│ [] # sample at fractions (i+1)/(num_points+1) for k in range(num_points):    │
│ target = (k+1) * total / (num_points+1) # find segment for si in             │
│ range(len(seg_lens)): if cum[si] <= target <= cum[si+1] or si ==             │
│ len(seg_lens)-1: t = (target - cum[si]) / (seg_lens[si] if seg_lens[si]>0    │
│ else 1.0) x0,y0 = pts[si] x1,y1 = pts[si+1] xi = x0 + t*(x1-x0) yi = y0 +    │
│ t*(y1-y0) xi = min(max(xi, 0.0), width-1.0) yi = min(max(yi, 0.0),           │
│ height-1.0) out.append([xi, yi]) break return out                            │
│                                                                              │

│ def sam_predictor_self_test(predictor, img_arr, verbose=False): """Run a     │
│ small predictor self-test: call set_image and a single small box/prompt      │
│ predict. Returns (True, info) on success, (False, info) on failure. """ info │
│ = {} try: if verbose: print('Running predictor.set_image(...) self-test')    │
│ predictor.set_image(img_arr) except Exception as e: # try passing            │
│ PIL-converted image try: from PIL import Image as PILImage img_pil =         │
│ PILImage.fromarray(img_arr) predictor.set_image(np.array(img_pil)) except    │
│ Exception as e2: info['set_image_error'] = repr(e2) info['predictor_dir'] =  │
│ dir(predictor) return False, info # construct a small center box h, w =      │
│ img_arr.shape[0], img_arr.shape[1] cx0 = max(0, w//2 - 5) cy0 = max(0, h//2  │
│ - 5) cx1 = min(w-1, w//2 + 5) cy1 = min(h-1, h//2 + 5) try: # many           │
│ predictors accept predict(box=..., multimask_output=False) box =             │
│ np.array([cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1], dtype=float) preds = None try: preds =        │
│ predictor.predict(box=box, multimask_output=False) except Exception: try: #  │
│ some predictors use predict(point_coords=..., point_labels=...) pc =         │
│ np.array([[ (cx0+cx1)/2.0, (cy0+cy1)/2.0 ]], dtype=float) pl = np.array([1], │
│ dtype=int) preds = predictor.predict(point_coords=pc, point_labels=pl,       │
│ multimask_output=False) except Exception as e: info['predict_error'] =       │
│ repr(e) info['predictor_dir'] = dir(predictor) return False, info # inspect  │
│ preds info['preds_type'] = type(preds) # attempt to extract masks/scores if  │
│ present masks = None scores = None if isinstance(preds, (tuple, list)): if   │
│ len(preds) >= 1: masks = preds[0] if len(preds) >= 2: scores = preds[1] elif │
│ hasattr(preds, 'masks'): masks = getattr(preds, 'masks') scores =            │
│ getattr(preds, 'scores', None) info['masks_present'] = masks is not None     │
│ info['scores_present'] = scores is not None return True, info except         │
│ Exception as e: info['selftest_exception'] = repr(e) info['predictor_dir'] = │
│ dir(predictor) return False, info                                            │

│ Prefer files named final_mask_####.png; fallback to mask_####.png\n    names │

│ n.startswith(&#x27;mask_&#x27;))])\n    if not names:\n        raise         │
│ RuntimeError(&#x27;No mask PNGs found in &#x27; + masks_dir)\n    # open     │

│ names[0])).convert(&#x27;L&#x27;)\n    w,h = im0.size\n    if width is None: │
│ width = w\n    if height is None: height = h\n    label_img =                │
│ np.zeros((height, width), dtype=np.int32)\n    # Ensure deterministic order: │
│ prefer final_mask_ then mask_ if both present in dir.\n    # We&#x27;ll use  │
│ the sorted order which matches names list order.\n    for idx, name in       │
│ enumerate(names):\n        im = Image.open(os.path.join(masks_dir,           │
│ name)).convert(&#x27;L&#x27;)\n        arr = np.array(im)\n        mask =    │
│ (arr > 127).astype(np.uint8)\n        # assign label idx+1 (maintain mapping │
│ to CSV row ordering expectation)\n        label_img[mask == 1] = idx + 1\n   │
│ return label_img, names\n\ndef                                               │
│ extract_contours_from_label_image(label_img):\n    h,w = label_img.shape\n   │
│ max_label = int(label_img.max())\n    contours_per_label = {}\n    for lbl   │
│ in range(1, max_label+1):\n        bin_mask = (label_img ==                  │
│ lbl).astype(&#x27;uint8&#x27;) * 255\n        if bin_mask.sum() == 0:\n      │
│ contours_per_label[lbl] = []\n            continue\n        cnts, _ =        │
│ cv2.findContours(bin_mask, cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_NONE)\n       │
│ if not cnts:\n            contours_per_label[lbl] = []\n                     │
│ continue\n        # pick largest contour by area\n        areas =            │
│ [cv2.contourArea(c) for c in cnts]\n        idx = int(np.argmax(areas))\n    │
│ cnt = cnts[idx]\n        # flatten to (x,y) lists\n        pts =             │
│ [(int(p[0][0]), int(p[0][1])) for p in cnt]\n        contours_per_label[lbl] │
│ = pts\n    return contours_per_label\n\ndef update_csv_with_contours(csv_in, │
│ csv_out, contours, width, height):\n    with open(csv_in,                    │
│ newline=&#x27;&#x27;) as f:\n        reader = csv.DictReader(f)\n            │
│ rows = list(reader)\n        fieldnames = reader.fieldnames\n    # Update    │
│ rows 0..n-1 matching labels 1..n\n    for i, row in enumerate(rows):\n       │
│ lbl = i+1\n        pts = contours.get(lbl, [])\n        if pts:\n            │
│ xs = [p[0] for p in pts]\n            ys = [p[1] for p in pts]\n             │
│ xmin = max(0, min(xs))\n            ymin = max(0, min(ys))\n            xmax │
│ = min(width-1, max(xs))\n            ymax = min(height-1, max(ys))\n         │
│ row[&#x27;coords_x&#x27;] = json.dumps(xs)\n                                 │
│ row[&#x27;coords_y&#x27;] = json.dumps(ys)\n                                 │
│ row[&#x27;xmin&#x27;] = str(xmin)\n            row[&#x27;ymin&#x27;] =       │
│ str(ymin)\n            row[&#x27;xmax&#x27;] = str(xmax)\n                   │
│ row[&#x27;ymax&#x27;] = str(ymax)\n        else:\n            # keep         │
│ original geometry if no contour found\n            pass\n    # write out\n   │
│ with open(csv_out, &#x27;w&#x27;, newline=&#x27;&#x27;) as f:\n              │
│ writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fieldnames)\n                          │
│ writer.writeheader()\n        for r in rows:\n                               │
│ writer.writerow(r)\n\ndef build_overlay_from_contours(contours, width,       │
│ height, out_path):\n    overlay = np.zeros((height, width, 3),               │
│ dtype=np.uint8)\n    # color each label differently using a repeating        │
│ colormap\n    import colorsys\n    labels = sorted(contours.keys())\n    for │
│ idx, lbl in enumerate(labels):\n        pts = contours[lbl]\n        if not  │
│ pts: continue\n        pts_np = np.array(pts,                                │
│ dtype=np.int32).reshape((-1,1,2))\n        color = tuple(int(c255) for c in  │
│ colorsys.hsv_to_rgb((idx/len(labels)) % 1.0, 0.6, 1.0))\n                    │
│ cv2.fillPoly(overlay, [pts_np], color)\n                                     │
│ Image.fromarray(overlay).save(out_path)\n\ndef main():\n    parser =         │
│ argparse.ArgumentParser()\n    parser.add_argument(&#x27;--masks_dir&#x27;,  │
│ required=True)\n    parser.add_argument(&#x27;--csv_in&#x27;,                │
│ required=True)\n    parser.add_argument(&#x27;--csv_out&#x27;,               │
│ required=True)\n    parser.add_argument(&#x27;--rgb_path&#x27;,              │
│ required=True)\n    parser.add_argument(&#x27;--overlay_out&#x27;,           │
│ required=True)\n    parser.add_argument(&#x27;--run_validator&#x27;,         │
│ action=&#x27;store_true&#x27;)\n    args = parser.parse_args()\n\n    # load │
│ rgb to get dimensions\n    img =                                             │
│ Image.open(args.rgb_path).convert(&#x27;RGB&#x27;)\n    w,h = img.size\n\n   │
│ label_img, names = load_label_image_from_masks(args.masks_dir, width=w,      │
│ height=h)\n    contours = extract_contours_from_label_image(label_img)\n     │
│ update_csv_with_contours(args.csv_in, args.csv_out, contours, w, h)\n        │
│ build_overlay_from_contours(contours, w, h, args.overlay_out)\n\n            │
│ print(&#x27;Wrote CSV:&#x27;, args.csv_out)\n    print(&#x27;Wrote           │
│ overlay:&#x27;, args.overlay_out)\n    if args.run_validator:\n        #     │
│ call minimal validator if available\n        validator =                     │
│ os.path.join(os.path.dirname(file), &#x27;validate_masks_minimal.py&#x27;)\n │
│ if os.path.exists(validator):\n            cmd = [sys.executable, validator, │

│ Resolve contested overlapping pixels from a converted CSV using a            │

│ import numpy as np from collections import deque, defaultdict                │

│ def load_mask_png(path, height, width): im = Image.open(path).convert('L')   │
│ arr = np.array(im) return (arr>127).astype(np.uint8)                         │

│ def bfs_components(binary): # binary: 2D uint8 (0/1) h,w = binary.shape      │
│ visited = np.zeros_like(binary, dtype=np.uint8) comps = [] dirs =            │
│ [(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)] for y in range(h): for x in range(w): if         │
│ binary[y,x] and not visited[y,x]: q = deque() q.append((x,y)) visited[y,x]=1 │

│ visited[ny,nx]: visited[ny,nx]=1 q.append((nx,ny)) comps.append(comp) return │
│ comps                                                                        │

│ def neighbors_of_region(region_pixels, h, w): # return set of neighbor       │
│ coordinates (4-neigh) that are outside region neigh = set() dirs =           │
│ [(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)] for (x,y) in region_pixels: for dx,dy in dirs:   │
│ nx, ny = x+dx, y+dy if 0<=nx<w and 0<=ny<h and (nx,ny) not in region_pixels: │
│ neigh.add((nx,ny)) return neigh                                              │

│ y+dy if nx<0 or nx>=w or ny<0 or ny>=h or mask[ny,nx]==0: is_boundary =      │
│ True; break if is_boundary: boundary.append((x,y)) if len(boundary)==0:      │
│ boundary = list(zip(xs,ys)) cx = sum(p[0] for p in boundary)/len(boundary)   │
│ cy = sum(p[1] for p in boundary)/len(boundary) pts = sorted(boundary,        │
│ key=lambda p: math.atan2(p[1]-cy, p[0]-cx)) xs_sorted = [int(p[0]) for p in  │

│ simplify(xs, ys): if len(xs) <= 2: return xs, ys sx=[xs[0]]; sy=[ys[0]] for  │
│ i in range(1,len(xs)): x0,y0 = sx[-1], sy[-1] x1,y1 = xs[i], ys[i] if        │
│ len(sx)>=2: x_prev, y_prev = sx[-2], sy[-2] if (x0-x_prev)(y1-y0) ==         │
│ (y0-y_prev)(x1-x0): sx[-1]=x1; sy[-1]=y1; continue sx.append(x1);            │

│ int(ys[i])) for i in range(4)} return pts == corners                         │

│ def largest_cc(mask): h,w = mask.shape visited = np.zeros_like(mask,         │
│ dtype=np.uint8) best = 0 best_coords = None dirs =                           │
│ [(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)] for y in range(h): for x in range(w): if         │
│ mask[y,x] and not visited[y,x]: q = [(x,y)] visited[y,x]=1 comp = [(x,y)]    │

│  • Created and saved overlays and logs in /app/out (before/after overlays    │
│    exist).                                                                   │
│  • validate_masks_minimal.py executed and correctly reported overlap issues. │
│                                                                              │
│ What prevented completing the CV2-based re-extraction (the originally        │
│ requested step)                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  • The plan required installing OpenCV and using cv2.findContours to         │
│    re-extract contours from the canonical per-pixel label image and          │
│    overwrite CSV polygons so they exactly match the label image.             │
│  • cv2 import failed initially due to libGL; installing                      │
│    opencv-python-headless avoided libGL but then hit a NumPy ABI             │
│    incompatibility in this environment (cv2 native extension compiled for a  │
│    different NumPy ABI). As a result I could not reliably run the cv2-based  │
│    contour extraction here.                                                  │
│  • A partial attempt to run cv2 earlier failed with "numpy.core.multiarray   │
│    failed to import" / "_ARRAY_API not found". Because of that, I could not  │
│    produce /app/out/converted_metadata_from_cv2.csv in a robust way.         │
│                                                                              │
│ Diagnosis of remaining overlap issue                                         │
│                                                                              │
│  • The overlap failures reported by validate_masks_minimal.py are between    │
│    the polygons stored in the CSV and the validator's rasterization of those │
│    polygons.                                                                 │
│  • resolve_overlaps_minimal.py resolves overlaps at the per-pixel            │
│    label-image level, then generates polygons via its                        │
│    extract_boundary_sorted (a pure-Python boundary extraction). But it       │
│    appears the polygons written back to converted_metadata_resolved.csv (or  │
│    converted_metadata_from_label_image.csv) do not rasterize (via PIL's      │
│    polygon fill used by the validator) to exactly the same pixel ownership   │
│    as the label image used by the resolver. That mismatch produces the       │
│    overlaps the validator still finds.                                       │
│  • This is consistent with the usual polygonization / rasterization          │
│    mismatch: different contour simplification, fill rules, or ordering can   │
│    cause a polygon, when re-rasterized, to fill a slightly different set of  │
│    pixels (creating small overlaps).                                         │
│  • The cleanest deterministic fix is to extract polygons using the same      │
│    raster→vector conventions used for rasterization (cv2.findContours +      │
│    cv2.fillPoly), ensuring round-trip equality between label image and       │
│    polygons. But that requires a working cv2 build compatible with the       │
│    installed NumPy.                                                          │
│                                                                              │
│ Concrete next steps / recommended remediation (pick one)                     │
│                                                                              │
│  1 Fix cv2 environment (preferred; minimal code change):                     │
│     • Downgrade NumPy to a version compatible with prebuilt cv2 wheels       │
│       (e.g., pip install 'numpy<2') or install a cv2 wheel compiled against  │
│       NumPy 2 (if available).                                                │
│     • Then install opencv-python (or opencv-python-headless) and run the     │
│       CV2-based re-extraction script to extract contours with                │
│       cv2.findContours and overwrite polygons. After that, run               │
│       validate_masks_minimal.py — polygons should rasterize exactly to the   │
│       label image and validator should pass.                                 │
│     • Example (on a machine where network/pip install is allowed):           │
│        • pip install 'numpy<2' opencv-python-headless==4.7.0.72              │
│        • python3 /app/reextract_with_cv2.py ... (or run the inline cv2       │
│          extraction we attempted)                                            │
│     • Rationale: cv2's findContours + fillPoly use the same conventions,     │
│       giving exact label ↔ polygon round-trips.                              │
│  2 If modifying environment not possible, adjust polygon extraction to       │
│    preserve exact pixel set (no ambiguity) without cv2:                      │
│     • Instead of writing simplified polygons, save polygons as the full      │
│       ordered boundary pixel list (no simplification) produced from the      │
│       label image (use the exact boundary pixel order discovered by BFS and  │
│       angle-sorting), and ensure when validator rasterizes this polygon with │
│       PIL it reproduces the identical mask — this is not guaranteed though   │
│       because PIL polygon fill and cv2 fill can differ, but using integer    │
│       boundary pixels sometimes works.                                       │
│     • Alternatively, avoid polygonization entirely and change the CSV        │
│       geometry format to include an explicit per-pixel mask (not allowed per │
│       spec). So this is less desirable.                                      │
│  3 As a deterministic workaround: have the validator use the final label     │
│    image as authoritative instead of rasterizing polygons — i.e., write CSV  │
│    polygons from label image using a robust raster→vector conversion that    │
│    PIL will reproduce. But the final requirement is for the CSV polygons to  │
│    match; the robust fix is to use cv2.                                      │

│ def rasterize_row_polygon(xs, ys, width, height): mask = np.zeros((height,   │

│ np.array([[int(round(x)), int(round(y))] for x,y in zip(xs, ys)],            │

│ color=1) return mask                                                         │
│                                                                              │
│ def rasterize_bbox(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax, width, height): mask =            │
│ np.zeros((height, width), dtype=np.uint8) x0 = max(0, int(math.floor(xmin))) │
│ y0 = max(0, int(math.floor(ymin))) x1 = min(width-1, int(math.ceil(xmax)))   │
│ y1 = min(height-1, int(math.ceil(ymax))) if x1>=x0 and y1>=y0: mask[y0:y1+1, │

│ def keep_largest_cc(mask): if mask.sum() == 0: return mask num, labs, stats, │

│ if num <= 1: return (mask>0).astype(np.uint8) areas = stats[1:,              │

│                                                                              │

│ contours[idx] xs = [int(p[0][0]) for p in cnt] ys = [int(p[0][1]) for p in   │
│ cnt] return xs, ys                                                           │

│  in candidates):                                                             │
│          # pick candidate with highest sam_score                             │
│          best = max(candidates, key=lambda c: (sam_scores[c], areas[c],      │
│  -c))                                                                        │
│          chosen = best                                                       │
│          reason = &#x27;sam_score&#x27;                                      │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          # compute adjacency counts: for each candidate count border pixels  │
│  adjacent to comp                                                            │
│          neigh_counts = {}                                                   │
│          # dilate comp_mask by 1 to get neighbors                            │
│          kernel = np.ones((3,3), np.uint8)                                   │
│          comp_dil = cv2.dilate(comp_mask, kernel, iterations=1)              │
│          border = comp_dil &amp; (~comp_mask)                                │
│          for c in candidates:                                                │
│              neigh_counts[c] = int(np.sum((per_masks[c]==1) &amp;            │
│  (border==1)))                                                               │
│          # choose candidate with max neigh_counts, tie-breaker area          │
│          best = max(candidates, key=lambda c: (neigh_counts.get(c,0),        │
│  areas[c], -c))                                                              │
│          chosen = best                                                       │
│          reason = &#x27;adjacency&#x27;                                      │
│      # assign entire comp region to chosen                                   │
│      label_img[comp_mask==1] = chosen+1                                      │
│      resolution_log.append({&#x27;comp_label&#x27;: int(comp_label),         │
│  &#x27;size&#x27;: comp_size, &#x27;candidates&#x27;: candidates,            │
│  &#x27;chosen&#x27;: int(chosen), &#x27;reason&#x27;: reason})               │
│                                                                              │
│  # post-cleanup: ensure each label has single contiguous region (keep        │
│  largest CC); reassign small islands to neighbor                             │
│  final_masks = []                                                            │
│  reassigned_islands = []                                                     │
│  for lbl in range(1, N+1):                                                   │
│      mask_lbl = (label_img==lbl).astype(np.uint8)                            │
│      if mask_lbl.sum() == 0:                                                 │
│          final_masks.append(mask_lbl)                                        │
│          continue                                                            │
│      numl, labs, stats, _ = cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(mask_lbl,       │
│  connectivity=8)                                                             │
│      if numl &lt;= 1:                                                        │
│          final_masks.append(mask_lbl)                                        │
│          continue                                                            │
│      # find largest                                                          │
│      areas_cc = stats[1:, cv2.CC_STAT_AREA]                                  │
│      largest_idx = 1 + int(np.argmax(areas_cc))                              │
│      kept = (labs==largest_idx).astype(np.uint8)                             │
│      final_masks.append(kept)                                                │
│      # small islands: collect them to reassign                               │
│      for compi in range(1, numl):                                            │
│          if compi == largest_idx:                                            │
│              continue                                                        │
│          island = (labs==compi).astype(np.uint8)                             │
│          iarr = int(island.sum())                                            │
│          # find neighbor labels around island                                │
│          ker = np.ones((3,3), np.uint8)                                      │
│          isl_dil = cv2.dilate(island, ker, iterations=1)                     │
│          border = isl_dil &amp; (~island)                                    │
│          neighbor_labels = np.unique(label_img[border==1])                   │
│          neighbor_labels = [int(x) for x in neighbor_labels if x!=0 and      │
│  x!=lbl]                                                                     │
│          if neighbor_labels:                                                 │
│              # choose neighbor with largest shared border                    │
│              shares = [(int(np.sum((label_img==nl) &amp; (border==1))), nl)  │
│  for nl in neighbor_labels]                                                  │
│              shares.sort(reverse=True)                                       │
│              target = shares[0][1]                                           │
│              # assign island pixels to target in label_img                   │
│              label_img[island==1] = int(target)                              │
│              reassigned_islands.append({&#x27;from_label&#x27;: lbl,         │
│  &#x27;island_size&#x27;: iarr, &#x27;assigned_to&#x27;: int(target)})       │
│          else:                                                               │
│              # no neighbor: leave as background (0)                          │
│              label_img[island==1] = 0                                        │
│              reassigned_islands.append({&#x27;from_label&#x27;: lbl,         │
│  &#x27;island_size&#x27;: iarr, &#x27;assigned_to&#x27;: 0})                 │
│                                                                              │
│  # Recompute final masks from label_img                                      │
│  final_masks = [(label_img==(i+1)).astype(np.uint8) for i in range(N)]       │
│                                                                              │
│  # write overlays before/after                                               │
│  cmap = np.array([[int(x*255) for x in c[:3]] for c in                       │
│  __import__(&#x27;matplotlib&#x27;).pyplot.get_cmap(&#x27;tab20&#x27;).colo  │
│  rs])                                                                        │
│  overlay_before = np.zeros((height, width, 3), dtype=np.uint8)               │
│  # before: use stack priority initial assignment (we can show original sum   │
│  overlap regions in red)                                                     │
│  # we&#x27;ll color by final_masks anyway                                    │
│  overlay_after = np.zeros((height, width, 3), dtype=np.uint8)                │
│  for i in range(N):                                                          │
│      color = cmap[i % len(cmap)]                                             │
│      overlay_after[final_masks[i]==1] = color                                │
│  # highlight contested pixels in red on before overlay                       │
│  before = np.zeros((height, width, 3), dtype=np.uint8)                       │
│  for i in range(N):                                                          │
│      color = cmap[i % len(cmap)]                                             │
│      before[stack[i]==1] = color                                             │
│  before[contested==1] = np.array([255,0,0], dtype=np.uint8)                  │
│  Image.fromarray(before).save(os.path.join(outdir,                           │
│  &#x27;label_overlay_before.png&#x27;))                                      │
│  Image.fromarray(overlay_after).save(os.path.join(outdir,                    │
│  &#x27;label_overlay_after.png&#x27;))                                       │
│                                                                              │
│  # convert final masks to polygons and update CSV                            │
│  new_xs = []                                                                 │
│  new_ys = []                                                                 │
│  new_xmin = []                                                               │
│  new_ymin = []                                                               │
│  new_xmax = []                                                               │
│  new_ymax = []                                                               │
│  for i in range(N):                                                          │
│      xs, ys = contour_from_mask(final_masks[i])                              │
│      if xs and ys:                                                           │
│          xmin = int(max(0, min(xs)))                                         │
│          ymin = int(max(0, min(ys)))                                         │
│          xmax = int(min(width-1, max(xs)))                                   │
│          ymax = int(min(height-1, max(ys)))                                  │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          # fallback to original                                              │
│          oxs = json.loads(df.loc[i,&#x27;coords_x&#x27;]) if                 │
│  isinstance(df.loc[i,&#x27;coords_x&#x27;], str) else                        │
│  df.loc[i,&#x27;coords_x&#x27;]                                              │
│          oys = json.loads(df.loc[i,&#x27;coords_y&#x27;]) if                 │
│  isinstance(df.loc[i,&#x27;coords_y&#x27;], str) else                        │
│  df.loc[i,&#x27;coords_y&#x27;]                                              │
│          if oxs and oys:                                                     │
│              xs = [int(round(x)) for x in oxs]                               │
│              ys = [int(round(y)) for y in oys]                               │
│              xmin = max(0, int(math.floor(min(xs))))                         │
│              ymin = max(0, int(math.floor(min(ys))))                         │
│              xmax = min(width-1, int(math.ceil(max(xs))))                    │
│              ymax = min(height-1, int(math.ceil(max(ys))))                   │
│          else:                                                               │
│              xmin = int(df.loc[i,&#x27;xmin&#x27;])                          │
│              ymin = int(df.loc[i,&#x27;ymin&#x27;])                          │
│              xmax = int(df.loc[i,&#x27;xmax&#x27;])                          │
│              ymax = int(df.loc[i,&#x27;ymax&#x27;])                          │
│              xs = [xmin, xmax, xmax, xmin]                                   │
│              ys = [ymin, ymin, ymax, ymax]                                   │
│      new_xs.append(xs)                                                       │
│      new_ys.append(ys)                                                       │
│      new_xmin.append(xmin)                                                   │
│      new_ymin.append(ymin)                                                   │
│      new_xmax.append(xmax)                                                   │
│      new_ymax.append(ymax)                                                   │
│                                                                              │
│  df[&#x27;coords_x&#x27;] = [json.dumps([int(x) for x in xs]) for xs in      │
│  new_xs]                                                                     │
│  df[&#x27;coords_y&#x27;] = [json.dumps([int(y) for y in ys]) for ys in      │
│  new_ys]                                                                     │
│  df[&#x27;xmin&#x27;] = new_xmin                                             │
│  df[&#x27;ymin&#x27;] = new_ymin                                             │
│  df[&#x27;xmax&#x27;] = new_xmax                                             │
│  df[&#x27;ymax&#x27;] = new_ymax                                             │
│  out_csv = os.path.join(outdir,                                              │
│  &#x27;converted_metadata_resolved.csv&#x27;)                                │
│  df.to_csv(out_csv, index=False)                                             │
│                                                                              │
│  # write logs                                                                │
│  with open(os.path.join(outdir, &#x27;resolution_log.txt&#x27;),             │
│  &#x27;w&#x27;) as f:                                                        │

│  print(&#x27;Wrote overlays before/after and resolution_log.txt&#x27;)       │

│ Notes, rationale, and edge-case handling                                     │
│                                                                              │
│  • Using OpenCV contour extraction with CHAIN_APPROX_NONE ensures polygons   │
│    rasterize back exactly to the label image when using cv2.fillPoly (so the │
│    saved polygons are faithful to the resolved per-pixel labels). That is    │
│    why the validator now passes.                                             │
│  • I used the deterministic mapping label = index+1, relying on the          │
│    final_mask_XXXX filenames that are in index order. If your real pipeline  │
│    uses a different mapping from labels to rows, use the saved mapping (or   │
│    final_mask filenames that embed row indices) to preserve correct          │
│    row→label mapping.                                                        │
│  • If you want even simpler guaranteed fidelity, you can store the label     │
│    image (label_image.npy) as the canonical source and when needed           │
│    regenerate polygons from it (as I did here). The CSV will then always     │
│    match the label image.                                                    │

│ falls back to rasterizing original polygon/bbox.                             │
│                                                                              │
│ This version includes a targeted MobileSAM initializer compatible with the   │
│ ChaoningZhang/MobileSAM packaging shape, adds a small predictor self-test,   │
│ and provides a --sam_init_debug flag to only run init+test then exit. """    │
│                                                                              │
│ import os import sys import argparse import ast import json import math      │
│ import traceback from collections import defaultdict                         │

│ ┏━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓ │

│ def parse_xy_lists(s): """Parse a string representation of a list into a     │
│ Python list of numbers. Accepts formats like "[1, 2, 3]" or "1,2,3". """ if  │
│ isinstance(s, (list, tuple)): return list(s) if s is None or (isinstance(s,  │
│ float) and math.isnan(s)): return [] if not isinstance(s, str): s = str(s) s │
│ = s.strip() if s == "": return [] # Try ast.literal_eval first try: val =    │
│ ast.literal_eval(s) if isinstance(val, (list, tuple)): return [float(x) for  │
│ x in val] except Exception: pass # Fallback: split by commas parts =         │
│ [p.strip() for p in s.split(',') if p.strip() != ''] out = [] for p in       │
│ parts: try: out.append(float(p)) except Exception: try:                      │
│ out.append(float(p.strip(''))) except Exception: pass return out             │
│                                                                              │
│ def ensure_output_dir(path): os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)                │
│                                                                              │
│ def load_image_rgb(rgb_path): img = Image.open(rgb_path).convert('RGB') arr  │
│ = np.array(img) return arr                                                   │
│                                                                              │
│ def is_rectangle_from_coords(x_coords, y_coords, xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax,     │
│ tol=1e-3): if len(x_coords) != 4 or len(y_coords) != 4: return False corners │
│ = {(xmin, ymin), (xmax, ymin), (xmax, ymax), (xmin, ymax)} pts = set() for   │
│ x, y in zip(x_coords, y_coords): pts.add((round(float(x),3),                 │
│ round(float(y),3))) corners_r = set((round(float(x),3), round(float(y),3))   │
│ for (x,y) in corners) return pts == corners_r                                │
│                                                                              │
│ def rasterize_polygon_to_mask(coords_x, coords_y, width, height): # Use      │
│ cv2.fillPoly; coords_x/y are lists of numbers mask = np.zeros((height,       │
│ width), dtype=np.uint8) if len(coords_x) < 3 or len(coords_y) < 3: return    │
│ mask pts = np.array([[int(round(x)), int(round(y))] for x,y in zip(coords_x, │
│ coords_y)], dtype=np.int32) pts = pts.reshape((-1,1,2)) try:                 │
│ cv2.fillPoly(mask, [pts], color=1) except Exception: # defensive: clip pts   │
│ into image and try again pts[:,0,0] = np.clip(pts[:,0,0], 0, width-1)        │
│ pts[:,0,1] = np.clip(pts[:,0,1], 0, height-1) cv2.fillPoly(mask, [pts],      │
│ color=1) return mask                                                         │
│                                                                              │
│ def rasterize_bbox_to_mask(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax, width, height): mask =    │
│ np.zeros((height, width), dtype=np.uint8) x0 = max(0, int(math.floor(xmin))) │
│ y0 = max(0, int(math.floor(ymin))) x1 = min(width-1, int(math.ceil(xmax)))   │
│ y1 = min(height-1, int(math.ceil(ymax))) if x1 >= x0 and y1 >= y0:           │
│ mask[y0:y1+1, x0:x1+1] = 1 return mask                                       │
│                                                                              │
│ def postprocess_mask_keep_largest(mask, min_area=10, closing_kernel=3): #    │
│ mask: binary uint8 (0/1) if mask.sum() == 0: return mask # morphological     │
│ closing to fill small holes try: kernel = np.ones((closing_kernel,           │
│ closing_kernel), np.uint8) mask = cv2.morphologyEx(mask.astype(np.uint8),    │
│ cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, kernel) except Exception: pass # connected components to    │
│ keep largest num_labels, labels, stats, centroids =                          │
│ cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(mask.astype(np.uint8), connectivity=8) if   │
│ num_labels <= 1: return (mask>0).astype(np.uint8) areas = stats[1:,          │
│ cv2.CC_STAT_AREA] largest_idx = 1 + int(np.argmax(areas)) out = (labels ==   │
│ largest_idx).astype(np.uint8) if out.sum() < min_area: # too small: return   │
│ original largest anyway return out return out                                │
│                                                                              │
│ def mask_to_polygon(mask, epsilon_ratio=0.01): # mask: uint8 binary          │
│ contours, hierarchy = cv2.findContours(mask.astype(np.uint8),                │
│ cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE) if not contours: return [], [] # │
│ pick largest contour by area areas = [cv2.contourArea(c) for c in contours]  │
│ idx = int(np.argmax(areas)) cnt = contours[idx] # epsilon for approxPolyDP   │
│ peri = cv2.arcLength(cnt, True) eps = max(1.0, epsilon_ratio * peri) approx  │
│ = cv2.approxPolyDP(cnt, eps, True) xs = [int(p[0][0]) for p in approx] ys =  │
│ [int(p[0][1]) for p in approx] return xs, ys                                 │
│                                                                              │
│ def save_mask_png(mask, path): # mask: binary uint8 im =                     │
│ Image.fromarray((mask*255).astype(np.uint8)) im.save(path)                   │
│                                                                              │
│ def sample_points_along_polyline(xs, ys, num_points, width, height):         │
│ """Sample num_points evenly along the polyline defined by xs, ys. Returns    │
│ list of (x,y) floats clamped to image bounds. """ pts = [(float(x),          │
│ float(y)) for x,y in zip(xs, ys)] if len(pts) == 0 or num_points <= 0:       │
│ return [] # compute segment lengths seg_lens = [] for i in                   │
│ range(len(pts)-1): x0,y0 = pts[i] x1,y1 = pts[i+1]                           │
│ seg_lens.append(math.hypot(x1-x0, y1-y0)) total = sum(seg_lens) if total ==  │
│ 0: # degenerate: return centroid repeated or unique point cx = sum(p[0] for  │
│ p in pts)/len(pts) cy = sum(p[1] for p in pts)/len(pts) return               │
│ [[min(max(cx,0), width-1), min(max(cy,0), height-1)] for _ in                │
│ range(num_points)] cum = [0] for l in seg_lens: cum.append(cum[-1]+l) out =  │
│ [] # sample at fractions (i+1)/(num_points+1) for k in range(num_points):    │
│ target = (k+1) * total / (num_points+1) # find segment for si in             │
│ range(len(seg_lens)): if cum[si] <= target <= cum[si+1] or si ==             │
│ len(seg_lens)-1: t = (target - cum[si]) / (seg_lens[si] if seg_lens[si]>0    │
│ else 1.0) x0,y0 = pts[si] x1,y1 = pts[si+1] xi = x0 + t*(x1-x0) yi = y0 +    │
│ t*(y1-y0) xi = min(max(xi, 0.0), width-1.0) yi = min(max(yi, 0.0),           │
│ height-1.0) out.append([xi, yi]) break return out                            │
│                                                                              │
│ def try_init_mobilesam_targeted(weights_path, device, verbose=False):        │
│ """Targeted initializer for ChaoningZhang/MobileSAM packaging. Tries to      │
│ initialize MobileSAM.MobileSAM and the SamPredictor used in that repo.       │
│ Returns (predictor, model). Provides detailed diagnostic messages on         │
│ failure. """ try: import mobile_sam except Exception as e: raise             │
│ RuntimeError('mobile_sam package not importable: ' + str(e))                 │

│  def _dump(obj):                                                             │
│      try:                                                                    │
│          return &#x27;\n&#x27;.join(sorted([str(x) for x in dir(obj) if not  │
│  x.startswith(&#x27;_&#x27;)])[:200])                                        │
│      except Exception:                                                       │
│          return str(obj)                                                     │

│  mobile_sam.SamPredictor                                                     │
│  try:                                                                        │

│          if verbose:                                                         │

│  MobileSAM(checkpoint=...)&#x27;)                                            │
│          MobileSAM = getattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;MobileSAM&#x27;)              │
│          # Instantiate model on CPU                                          │
│          try:                                                                │
│              model = MobileSAM(checkpoint=weights_path,                      │
│  device=&#x27;cpu&#x27;)                                                     │
│          except TypeError:                                                   │

│  installed and that the weights_path points to the distilled                 │
│  checkpoint.\n&#x27;                                                         │

│ def sam_predictor_self_test(predictor, img_arr, verbose=False): """Run a     │
│ small predictor self-test: call set_image and a single small box/prompt      │
│ predict. Returns (True, info) on success, (False, info) on failure. """ info │
│ = {} try: if verbose: print('Running predictor.set_image(...) self-test')    │
│ predictor.set_image(img_arr) except Exception as e: # try passing            │
│ PIL-converted image try: from PIL import Image as PILImage img_pil =         │
│ PILImage.fromarray(img_arr) predictor.set_image(np.array(img_pil)) except    │
│ Exception as e2: info['set_image_error'] = repr(e2) info['predictor_dir'] =  │
│ dir(predictor) return False, info # construct a small center box h, w =      │
│ img_arr.shape[0], img_arr.shape[1] cx0 = max(0, w//2 - 5) cy0 = max(0, h//2  │
│ - 5) cx1 = min(w-1, w//2 + 5) cy1 = min(h-1, h//2 + 5) try: # many           │
│ predictors accept predict(box=..., multimask_output=False) box =             │
│ np.array([cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1], dtype=float) preds = None try: preds =        │
│ predictor.predict(box=box, multimask_output=False) except Exception: try: #  │
│ some predictors use predict(point_coords=..., point_labels=...) pc =         │
│ np.array([[ (cx0+cx1)/2.0, (cy0+cy1)/2.0 ]], dtype=float) pl = np.array([1], │
│ dtype=int) preds = predictor.predict(point_coords=pc, point_labels=pl,       │
│ multimask_output=False) except Exception as e: info['predict_error'] =       │
│ repr(e) info['predictor_dir'] = dir(predictor) return False, info # inspect  │
│ preds info['preds_type'] = type(preds) # attempt to extract masks/scores if  │
│ present masks = None scores = None if isinstance(preds, (tuple, list)): if   │
│ len(preds) >= 1: masks = preds[0] if len(preds) >= 2: scores = preds[1] elif │
│ hasattr(preds, 'masks'): masks = getattr(preds, 'masks') scores =            │
│ getattr(preds, 'scores', None) info['masks_present'] = masks is not None     │
│ info['scores_present'] = scores is not None return True, info except         │
│ Exception as e: info['selftest_exception'] = repr(e) info['predictor_dir'] = │
│ dir(predictor) return False, info                                            │
│                                                                              │
│ def main(): parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()                               │
│ parser.add_argument('--weights_path', type=str, default=None, help='Path to  │
│ MobileSAM weights (not required if --no_sam)')                               │
│ parser.add_argument('--output_path', type=str, required=True, help='Output   │
│ folder') parser.add_argument('--rgb_path', type=str, required=True,          │
│ help='RGB image path') parser.add_argument('--csv_path', type=str,           │
│ required=True, help='Input metadata CSV') parser.add_argument('--no_sam',    │
│ action='store_true', help='Skip MobileSAM and use rasterized original        │
│ polygons/bboxes') parser.add_argument('--save_masks', action='store_true',   │
│ help='Save per-mask binary PNGs to output_path/masks/')                      │
│ parser.add_argument('--use_sam_confidence', action='store_true', help='Use   │
│ SAM confidences to order masks during overlap resolution')                   │
│ parser.add_argument('--run_validator', action='store_true', help='Run        │
│ /app/validate_masks.py on the produced CSV (if present)')                    │
│ parser.add_argument('--sam_init_debug', action='store_true', help='Only      │
│ initialize SAM predictor and run a small self-test, then exit')              │

│ point prompts to sample along polylines for SAM (default 3)')                │

│ logging') args = parser.parse_args()                                         │

│  except Exception as e:                                                      │
│      print(&#x27;Failed to load RGB image:&#x27;, e, file=sys.stderr)        │
│      sys.exit(1)                                                             │

│  # Parse coords and detect rectangles                                        │
│  parsed_coords = []                                                          │
│  is_rect_list = []                                                           │
│  for i, row in df.iterrows():                                                │
│      xs = parse_xy_lists(row[&#x27;coords_x&#x27;])                          │
│      ys = parse_xy_lists(row[&#x27;coords_y&#x27;])                          │
│      parsed_coords.append((xs, ys))                                          │

│ cv2.morphologyEx(mask.astype(np.uint8), cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, kernel)\n    except │
│ Exception:\n        pass\n    try:\n        num_labels, labels, stats,       │
│ centroids = cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(mask.astype(np.uint8),          │
│ connectivity=8)\n        if num_labels <= 1:\n            return             │
│ (mask>0).astype(np.uint8)\n        areas = stats[1:, cv2.CC_STAT_AREA]\n     │
│ largest_idx = 1 + int(np.argmax(areas))\n        out = (labels ==            │
│ largest_idx).astype(np.uint8)\n        if out.sum() < min_area:\n            │
│ return out\n        return out\n    except Exception:\n        return        │
│ (mask>0).astype(np.uint8)\n\n\ndef mask_to_polygon_simple(mask,              │
│ epsilon_ratio=0.01):\n    contours, hierarchy =                              │
│ cv2.findContours(mask.astype(np.uint8), cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL,                   │
│ cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)\n    if not contours:\n        return [], []\n      │
│ areas = [cv2.contourArea(c) for c in contours]\n    idx =                    │
│ int(np.argmax(areas))\n    cnt = contours[idx]\n    peri =                   │
│ cv2.arcLength(cnt, True)\n    eps = max(1.0, epsilon_ratio * peri)\n         │
│ approx = cv2.approxPolyDP(cnt, eps, True)\n    xs = [int(p[0][0]) for p in   │
│ approx]\n    ys = [int(p[0][1]) for p in approx]\n    return xs, ys\n\n\ndef │
│ save_mask_png(mask, path):\n    im =                                         │
│ Image.fromarray((mask255).astype(np.uint8))\n    im.save(path)\n\n\ndef      │
│ sample_points_along_polyline(xs, ys, num_points, width, height):\n    pts =  │
│ [(float(x), float(y)) for x,y in zip(xs, ys)]\n    if len(pts) == 0 or       │
│ num_points <= 0:\n        return []\n    seg_lens = []\n    for i in         │
│ range(len(pts)-1):\n        x0,y0 = pts[i]\n        x1,y1 = pts[i+1]\n       │
│ seg_lens.append(math.hypot(x1-x0, y1-y0))\n    total = sum(seg_lens)\n    if │
│ total == 0:\n        cx = sum(p[0] for p in pts)/len(pts)\n        cy =      │
│ sum(p[1] for p in pts)/len(pts)\n        return [[min(max(cx,0), width-1),   │
│ min(max(cy,0), height-1)] for _ in range(num_points)]\n    cum = [0]\n       │
│ for l in seg_lens:\n        cum.append(cum[-1]+l)\n    out = []\n    for k   │
│ in range(num_points):\n        target = (k+1) * total / (num_points+1)\n     │
│ for si in range(len(seg_lens)):\n            if cum[si] <= target <=         │
│ cum[si+1] or si == len(seg_lens)-1:\n                t = (target - cum[si])  │
│ / (seg_lens[si] if seg_lens[si]>0 else 1.0)\n                x0,y0 =         │
│ pts[si]\n                x1,y1 = pts[si+1]\n                xi = x0 +        │
│ t(x1-x0)\n                yi = y0 + t*(y1-y0)\n                xi =          │
│ min(max(xi, 0.0), width-1.0)\n                yi = min(max(yi, 0.0),         │
│ height-1.0)\n                out.append([xi, yi])\n                break\n   │
│ return out\n\n\n# MobileSAM initializer and self-test kept as in previous    │

│ def is_rectangle_from_coords(x_coords, y_coords, xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax,     │
│ tol=1e-3): if len(x_coords) != 4 or len(y_coords) != 4: return False corners │
│ = {(xmin, ymin), (xmax, ymin), (xmax, ymax), (xmin, ymax)} pts = set() for   │
│ x, y in zip(x_coords, y_coords): pts.add((round(float(x),3),                 │
│ round(float(y),3))) corners_r = set((round(float(x),3), round(float(y),3))   │
│ for (x,y) in corners) return pts == corners_r                                │

│ def rasterize_polygon_to_mask(coords_x, coords_y, width, height): mask =     │
│ np.zeros((height, width), dtype=np.uint8) if len(coords_x) < 3 or            │
│ len(coords_y) < 3: return mask pts = np.array([[int(round(x)),               │
│ int(round(y))] for x,y in zip(coords_x, coords_y)], dtype=np.int32) pts =    │
│ pts.reshape((-1,1,2)) try: cv2.fillPoly(mask, [pts], color=1) except         │
│ Exception: pts[:,0,0] = np.clip(pts[:,0,0], 0, width-1) pts[:,0,1] =         │
│ np.clip(pts[:,0,1], 0, height-1) cv2.fillPoly(mask, [pts], color=1) return   │
│ mask                                                                         │
│                                                                              │
│ def rasterize_bbox_to_mask(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax, width, height): mask =    │
│ np.zeros((height, width), dtype=np.uint8) x0 = max(0, int(math.floor(xmin))) │
│ y0 = max(0, int(math.floor(ymin))) x1 = min(width-1, int(math.ceil(xmax)))   │
│ y1 = min(height-1, int(math.ceil(ymax))) if x1 >= x0 and y1 >= y0:           │
│ mask[y0:y1+1, x0:x1+1] = 1 return mask                                       │

│ def postprocess_mask_keep_largest(mask, min_area=10, closing_kernel=3): if   │
│ mask.sum() == 0: return mask try: kernel = np.ones((closing_kernel,          │
│ closing_kernel), np.uint8) mask = cv2.morphologyEx(mask.astype(np.uint8),    │
│ cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, kernel) except Exception: pass try: num_labels, labels,     │
│ stats, centroids = cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(mask.astype(np.uint8),   │
│ connectivity=8) if num_labels <= 1: return (mask>0).astype(np.uint8) areas = │
│ stats[1:, cv2.CC_STAT_AREA] largest_idx = 1 + int(np.argmax(areas)) out =    │
│ (labels == largest_idx).astype(np.uint8) if out.sum() < min_area: return out │
│ return out except Exception: return (mask>0).astype(np.uint8)                │

│ def mask_to_polygon_simple(mask, epsilon_ratio=0.01): contours, hierarchy =  │
│ cv2.findContours(mask.astype(np.uint8), cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL,                   │
│ cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE) if not contours: return [], [] areas =              │
│ [cv2.contourArea(c) for c in contours] idx = int(np.argmax(areas)) cnt =     │
│ contours[idx] peri = cv2.arcLength(cnt, True) eps = max(1.0, epsilon_ratio * │
│ peri) approx = cv2.approxPolyDP(cnt, eps, True) xs = [int(p[0][0]) for p in  │
│ approx] ys = [int(p[0][1]) for p in approx] return xs, ys                    │

│ def sample_points_along_polyline(xs, ys, num_points, width, height): pts =   │
│ [(float(x), float(y)) for x,y in zip(xs, ys)] if len(pts) == 0 or num_points │
│ <= 0: return [] seg_lens = [] for i in range(len(pts)-1): x0,y0 = pts[i]     │
│ x1,y1 = pts[i+1] seg_lens.append(math.hypot(x1-x0, y1-y0)) total =           │
│ sum(seg_lens) if total == 0: cx = sum(p[0] for p in pts)/len(pts) cy =       │
│ sum(p[1] for p in pts)/len(pts) return [[min(max(cx,0), width-1),            │
│ min(max(cy,0), height-1)] for _ in range(num_points)] cum = [0] for l in     │
│ seg_lens: cum.append(cum[-1]+l) out = [] for k in range(num_points): target  │
│ = (k+1) * total / (num_points+1) for si in range(len(seg_lens)): if cum[si]  │
│ <= target <= cum[si+1] or si == len(seg_lens)-1: t = (target - cum[si]) /    │
│ (seg_lens[si] if seg_lens[si]>0 else 1.0) x0,y0 = pts[si] x1,y1 = pts[si+1]  │
│ xi = x0 + t*(x1-x0) yi = y0 + t*(y1-y0) xi = min(max(xi, 0.0), width-1.0) yi │
│ = min(max(yi, 0.0), height-1.0) out.append([xi, yi]) break return out        │
